u \simeq 3 	imes 10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Modeling yields fallback accretion energy injection $E_{m inj} \simeq 6 	imes 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and accreted mass $M_{m acc} \simeq 0.2\,M_\odot$ onto the newly formed black hole.
papers.problem: Investigating the physical origin of the rare double X-ray plateau, the abrupt decay accompanied by strong spectral softening, and the delayed, rapidly rising radio afterglow in the extragalactic fast X-ray transient EP251129a.
papers.method: Multi-wavelength data analysis combining EP-FXT, Swift-XRT, Chandra, optical facilities, and radio telescopes (VLA, e-MERLIN). Theoretical modeling incorporates millisecond magnetar spin-down dominated by gravitational wave radiation ($L_{\mathrm{EM}}(t) \simeq L_{\mathrm{em},0}(1+t/\tau_{c,\mathrm{gw}})^{-1}$), collapse to a black hole, dynamic forward shock in a wind medium ($\rho = A R^{-2}$) with a two-component off-axis jet (core angle $\theta_{\rm c}$, wing angle $\theta_{\rm j}$), and Blandford-Znajek fallback accretion energy injection ($L_{\rm BZ} \propto \dot{M}$).
papers.reason: The paper presents multi-wavelength observations and detailed theoretical modeling of EP251129a, an extragalactic fast X-ray transient (EFXT) exhibiting a unique double X-ray plateau, an off-axis afterglow, and evidence for a millisecond magnetar collapsing into a black hole with fallback energy injection.

papers.title: An Intermediate Mass Stripped Star in a 4.2-hour Orbit around a Compact Object
papers.result: The spectroscopic and photometric analysis shows the binary has orbital period $P \approx 4.2\text{ h}$, semi-amplitude $K = 151.4 \pm 2.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$, and circular orbit ($e < 0.045$ at 95% credible limit). The mass function $f(m) = \frac{P K^3}{2\pi G} = 0.062 \pm 0.003\,M_\odot$ yields a minimum companion mass $M_{2,\min} = 1.38 \pm 0.25\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$), with ellipsoidal light-curve modeling yielding a posterior peak of $M_2 = 1.58\,M_\odot$ (68% HDI: $[1.40 - 2.41]\,M_\odot$), identifying the companion as a compact object (most likely a neutron star). Chandra limits unabsorbed $2\text{--}7\text{ keV}$ X-ray luminosity to $L_{2-7\mathrm{keV}} < 7.8 \times 10^{32}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$. MESA evolutionary models show the system undergoes non-conservative Case BB mass transfer, exploding as an interaction-powered Type Ibn supernova and leaving a bound double neutron star that merges via gravitational waves in $\tau_{\rm delay} \approx 220\text{ Myr}$.
papers.problem: Identifying the intermediate evolutionary stage of double neutron star progenitors—specifically verifying the existence of stripped helium stars in tight orbits with a first-born compact object prior to Case BB mass transfer and core collapse—and determining companion nature against main-sequence or double-stripped star alternatives.
papers.method: Multi-epoch Magellan/MagE optical spectroscopy analyzed with *The Joker* for orbital parameter estimation and radial velocity semi-amplitude $K$; NTT/ULTRACAM high-speed photometry fitted with `ellc` for ellipsoidal modulation and orbital inclination constraints; Chandra ACIS-S and XMM-Newton X-ray upper limits evaluated against Bondi-Hoyle-Littleton accretion models ($L_{\mathrm{BHL}} = \epsilon \frac{G M_{\rm NS} \dot{M}_{\rm acc}}{R_{\rm NS}}$); and detailed MESA forward binary evolution tracking non-conservative Case BB mass transfer ($dj/dt = \gamma j$) through core collapse and gravitational-wave orbital decay.
papers.reason: This paper presents the discovery and characterization of DGL-3, an ultra-short-period ($P \approx 4.2\text{ h}$) binary in the SMC hosting an intermediate-mass stripped star and an unseen compact companion ($M_2 \approx 1.58\,M_\odot$), providing direct observational evidence of an immediate progenitor to a merging double neutron star system.

papers.title: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
papers.problem: Detecting electron antineutrinos from the cumulative past core-collapse supernovae (DSNB) against overwhelming backgrounds from atmospheric neutrino neutral-current and charged-current interactions as well as cosmic-ray muon spallation products.
papers.method: Analysis of 5003.0 days of Super-Kamiokande data (pure water and Gd-loaded SK-VI to SK-VIII phases) detecting inverse beta decay $\bar{\nu}_{e} + p \to e^{+} + n$ via an unbinned extended maximum likelihood fit across 6 subregions defined by Cherenkov angle $\theta_{\mathrm{C}}$ and tagged neutron multiplicity $N_{\rm n}$, incorporating machine learning for NC background rejection and an optimized threshold of $E_{\rm rec} = 11.5\text{ MeV}$ for $N_{\rm n} = 1$.
papers.reason: This work presents an observational indication of electron antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (DSNB) with Super-Kamiokande, yielding a 2.6 sigma tension with the null hypothesis and critical constraints on core-collapse supernova physics.

papers.title: The design and flight of the Payload for Ultrahigh Energy Observations (PUEO)
papers.result: PUEO successfully operated during a 23-day Antarctic flight with an average livetime fraction of $\sim 55\%$ (limited by thermal constraints to keep RFSoC temperatures below $80^\circ\mathrm{C}$), collecting $114,046,211$ RF trigger events. Ground-testing confirmed a $50\%$ trigger efficiency threshold at $\mathrm{SNR} = 1.4$ (over twice as sensitive as ANITA-IV). The multi-antenna GNSS orientation achieved smoothed pitch and roll standard deviations of $0.015^\circ$ and $0.024^\circ$, and heading residuals of $0.070^\circ$ after applying a spin-dependent time-lag correction $\text{Heading} = \text{Heading} - \tau\cdot\omega$.
papers.problem: Detecting extremely low flux ultrahigh-energy neutrinos ($E \gtrsim 1\text{ EeV}$) requires monitoring massive target volumes ($\sim 10^6\text{ km}^3$) of Antarctic ice while achieving trigger sensitivity near the thermal noise floor and discriminating genuine impulsively coherent Askaryan or air shower signals from anthropogenic RF interference and thermal fluctuations.
papers.method: PUEO incorporates a 96-horn dual-polarization main antenna array ($300-1200\text{ MHz}$) coupled to a real-time digital interferometric phased-array trigger implemented on 26 Xilinx RFSoC ZU47DR modules sampling at $3\text{ GSa/s}$, synthesizing 48 simultaneous coherent beams. Signal classification on the science computer uses coherent summation and Hilbert envelope energy concentration ($<10\%$ envelope duration containing $30\%$ total power for high-priority signals) alongside calibration pulses from ground pulsers and twin HiCal-3 balloons.
papers.reason: This paper presents the complete instrument architecture, flight performance, and calibration of PUEO, a premier balloon-borne experiment targeting ultrahigh-energy neutrinos ($E \gtrsim 1\text{ EeV}$) and cosmic rays via Askaryan radio impulses and EAS radio emission.

papers.title: SN Ares: A Strongly Lensed Type IIb Supernova at $\mathbf{z=1.276}$ with a Predicted 70-Year Time Delay
papers.result: SN Ares is spectroscopically classified as a Type IIb core-collapse supernova at $z_{\rm spec} = 1.276 \pm 0.002$ magnified by $\mu \approx 4.6 - 5.6$. Correcting for magnification (gain $\approx 1.9\;\mathrm{mag}$), its inferred intrinsic peak absolute magnitude is $M_{B,\max} \approx -17.1$ to $-17.9\;\mathrm{mag}$, consistent with binary progenitor systems like SN 1993J. Strong lensing modeling predicts two trailing images appearing $\sim 70-76\;\mathrm{yr}$ and $\sim 73-79\;\mathrm{yr}$ later.
papers.problem: Spectroscopically classifying high-redshift stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae and determining their intrinsic luminosities, phases, and time delays for cluster mass profile and cosmological constraints.
papers.method: Multi-model strong lensing reconstructions (Lenstool dPIE, glafic, AstroLensPy) constrained by 48 multiple images; rest-frame spectral template matching via NGSF; and multi-band light-curve fitting via MCMC using Gaussian processes parameterized by $\phi_{i} = \phi_{\rm ref} + \frac{t_{i}-t_{\rm ref}}{1+z_{\rm Ares}}$ and $m_{{\rm model},i} = m_{{\rm GP},f}(\phi_{i}) + \Delta m + K_{f} + A_{f}$.
papers.reason: This study reports the spectroscopic confirmation of a strongly lensed stripped-envelope Type IIb supernova at $z = 1.276$, providing physical luminosity constraints and multi-messenger/cosmological lensing time-delay predictions relevant to massive star progenitor evolution.

papers.title: Wolf-Rayet Stars in M33: The Impact of Stellar Crowding on Spectral Classification and Mass-Loss Diagnostics
papers.result: In M33, approximately 27% (33/123) of WR stars suffer moderate-to-severe continuum dilution ($F_{\rm WR} < 0.85$, with very crowded sources having $F_{\rm WR} \lesssim 0.50$ and optical equivalent widths diluted by a factor of $\gtrsim 2$). Because optically thin recombination line luminosities scale as $L_{\rm line} \propto \dot{M}^{2}$, uncorrected dilution severely underestimates or distorts $\dot{M}$. Keck/DEIMOS spectroscopy confirms the predicted dilution (${\rm EW_{Hecto}/EW_{DEIMOS}} = 0.55\text{--}0.90$) and yields wind velocity diagnostics of $v_{\rm FWHM} \approx 330\text{--}1025\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ for $\mathrm{He\ II}$ and blue absorption edge velocities $v_{\rm blue} \approx 700\text{--}1500\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ for $\mathrm{He\ I}\,\lambda 5876$.
papers.problem: Ground-based fiber spectroscopy (e.g., MMT/Hectospec with $1\farcs 5$ fibers corresponding to $\sim 4\text{ pc}$ in M33) blends WR targets with surrounding OB stars and diffuse ISM, diluting diagnostic emission lines and contaminating wind mass-loss diagnostics across metallicity gradients.
papers.method: Combined high-resolution ($0\farcs 1$) HST/PHATTER UV/optical photometry with a synthetic Gaussian fiber aperture model ($r_{\rm fib} = 0\farcs 75$, $\mathrm{FWHM} = 1\farcs 0$) to calculate the fractional WR flux contribution $F_i = \frac{f_i \cdot 10^{-0.4 m_i}}{\sum_j f_j \cdot 10^{-0.4 m_j}}$, established an empirical crowding metric based on centroid offset $d$ and magnitude difference $\Delta m_{12}$, and benchmarked ground spectra against narrow-slit Keck/DEIMOS spectroscopy.
papers.reason: Wolf-Rayet stars are key progenitors of stripped-envelope supernovae and potential central-engine-driven transients; quantifying how stellar crowding systematically dilutes emission-line equivalent widths and distorts inferred mass-loss rates $\dot{M}(Z)$ is crucial for establishing pre-supernova circumstellar medium (CSM) density profiles.

papers.title: Initial Conditions of Magnetized AGN Accretion Disks from Cloud Capture and Disruption
papers.result: The initial disk formed at the circularization radius $r_t$ is toroidally magnetically dominated with $\beta \ll 1$ and $|B_\phi| \gg |B_z|, |B_R|$. The disk scale height and accretion rate scale as $H_d/r_t \sim 4\alpha_{\rm cl,B}$ and $\dot{m} \sim 7\alpha_{\rm cl,B}(\Sigma_{\rm cl}/100\,M_\odot\,{\rm pc^{-2}})^{3/4}(M_{\rm cl}/10^7\,M_\odot)^{-1/4}(2/\tilde{v})$ for $M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$, where $\alpha_{\rm cl,B} \equiv E_{\rm mag}/E_{\rm grav}$. For $M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$, the tidal disruption gives $r_t \approx \xi(M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl})^{1/3}R_{\rm cl}$ and $H_d/r_t \sim (3\alpha_{\rm cl,B})^{1/4}(M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl})^{-1/4}$. In the post-encounter cutoff phase, the mass fallback follows a tidal-disruption-like power law $\dot{M} \propto t^{-5/3}$.
papers.problem: Standard accretion disk models (e.g., Shakura-Sunyaev, classical Bondi, or TDE disks) assume initially thermal-pressure-dominated gas (high $\beta$) and weak or dynamically unimportant seed magnetic fields, failing to describe the realistic formation and structure of outer accretion disks fed by turbulent, strongly magnetized interstellar clouds.
papers.method: Analytical formulation combining magnetic flux-freezing, supersonic turbulent energy conservation, and tidal disruption dynamics across three mass regimes ($M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm cl}$, $M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$, $M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$), evaluated with cloud mass functions $dN_{\rm cl}/dM_{\rm cl} \propto M_{\rm cl}^{-\gamma_{\rm cl}}$ and Larson scaling relations $v_{\rm cl} \propto R_{\rm cl}^{1/2}$.
papers.reason: The paper develops an analytical scaling framework for the initial outer conditions of AGN accretion disks formed by the capture and disruption of strongly magnetized, cold ISM clouds. It systematically predicts magnetically dominated (low-$\beta$), toroidally stretched disks and super-Eddington accretion rates across mass ratios $M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl}$, providing valuable initial/boundary conditions for compact object accretion and relativistic jet generation.

papers.title: Neutron Star--Primordial Black Hole Binaries: Dynamical Tides, Resonance Locking, and Gravitational Waves
papers.result: Resonance locking modifies the orbital evolution according to $\frac{\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb}}{\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb}^{\rm GW}} = \frac{I_{\rm orb}}{I_{\rm orb}-3I_{\rm NS}}$. If $I_{\rm orb} > 3I_{\rm NS}$ and $\Omega_{\rm orb} > \Omega_{\rm NS}$, tidal torques accelerate inspiral; conversely, when $I_{\rm orb} < 3I_{\rm NS}$ and $\Omega_{\rm NS} > \Omega_{\rm orb}$, angular momentum extracted from the NS spin drives an outspiral ($\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb} < 0$), preventing coalescence. During resonance locking, the pulsar braking index shifts to $n = \frac{11I_{\rm orb} - 21I_{\rm NS}}{3(I_{\rm orb} - 3I_{\rm NS})} \frac{\Omega_{\rm NS}}{\Omega_{\rm orb}}$, yielding $n \to \frac{11}{3}\frac{\Omega_{\rm NS}}{\Omega_{\rm orb}}$ in the limit $I_{\rm orb} \gg 3I_{\rm NS}$. Gravitational-wave detectability exhibits a weak scaling ${\rm SNR} \propto \eta^{1/2}$, enabling Cosmic Explorer to detect $M_{\rm BH} > 10^{-6}\,M_\odot$ at $10\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ (${\rm SNR} > 10$).
papers.problem: In extreme mass-ratio binaries with $M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm NS}$, standard equilibrium tides have negligible dissipation ($Q_{\rm tide} \gtrsim 10^3$, $\Omega_{\rm orb} t_{\rm tide} \sim 10^{16}$), leaving open the role of dynamical tides and mode resonance locks in driving or halting binary inspiral and altering pulsar braking indices.
papers.method: Coupled orbital and rotational post-Newtonian equations are evaluated with dynamical tidal torque $\tau_{\rm tide}$ and gravitational-wave backreaction $\tau_{\rm GW}$. Low-frequency NS modes ($1\,\mathrm{Hz} \lesssim \omega_X/2\pi \lesssim 200\,\mathrm{Hz}$) are modeled with non-linear forcing $f_{\rm ext} = -2\gamma \dot{a}_X - \beta a_X^3$. In the slowly varying envelope approximation $a_X = c_X e^{i\omega_X t}$ with $c_X = R e^{i\theta}$, mode evolution is governed by $\dot{R} = -\gamma R + \frac{A_X}{2\omega_X}\sin(\theta - \delta\phi)$ and $\dot{\theta} = \frac{3\beta}{8\omega_X}R^2 + \frac{A_X}{2\omega_X R}\cos(\theta - \delta\phi)$, shifting the resonance frequency by $\omega_X' = \omega_X + \frac{3\beta}{8\omega_X}R^2$.
papers.reason: This paper investigates how dynamical tides and resonance locking between neutron star internal oscillation modes and orbiting sub-solar mass primordial black holes govern orbital evolution and modify pulsar timing observables.

papers.title: Fast Outflow Driven from the Magnetically Arrested Disc
papers.result: Magnetically driven outflows from MADs smoothly traverse slow-magnetosonic, Alfvén, and fast-magnetosonic critical points, attaining mildly relativistic velocities ($v_{\rm p} \gtrsim 0.1c - 0.3c$) from inner disc streamlines ($R \lesssim 20 R_{\rm in}$, where $R_{\rm in}=6R_{\rm g}=6GM/c^2$) with distinct radial velocity stratification. Owing to high magnetization and low mass loading, the dimensionless magnetic lever arm reaches $\tilde{l} = (R_{\rm A}/R)^2 \sim 10 - 100$, allowing an outflow mass-loss rate of $\dot{M}_{\rm w} \simeq 0.14 \dot{M}_{\rm acc}$ to remove roughly $55\%$ of the disc angular momentum ($J_{\rm w} \simeq 0.55 J_{\rm acc}$).
papers.problem: Accounting for the acceleration and mass-loading of ultra-fast outflows (UFOs, $v \sim 0.1c-0.7c$) in highly ionized inner accretion flows around black holes where radiative line driving fails.
papers.method: Steady, axisymmetric trans-magnetosonic MHD outflow framework along prescribed magnetic field surfaces $\Phi=[(R/R_{\rm in})^2+(1+|z/R_{\rm in}|)^2]^{1/2}-(1+|z/R_{\rm in}|)$ with polytropic equation of state $P=K\rho^\gamma$ ($\gamma=1.4, 1.5$), adopting disc surface boundary conditions calibrated from GRMHD MAD simulations (geometric thickness $H/R \simeq 0.3$, sub-Keplerian rotation $f_\Omega = \Omega/\Omega_{\rm K} < 1$, and magnetization $\beta_{z_{\rm h}} \lesssim 1$).
papers.reason: The paper develops a semi-analytic magnetocentrifugal outflow model rooted in magnetically arrested discs (MADs) calibrated by GRMHD boundary conditions, addressing ultra-fast outflow (UFO) generation where radiation line-driving fails, which directly informs high-energy compact object accretion, relativistic jet sheath environments, and angular momentum transport.

papers.title: PeV Diffuse Neutrinos from Magnetically Arrested Disks in Low-Luminosity Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.problem: Constraining the contribution of radiatively inefficient accretion flows in magnetically arrested disk (MAD) states within LLAGNs to the diffuse astrophysical PeV neutrino background observed by IceCube.
papers.method: Modeling particle acceleration and non-thermal proton injection with power-law index $s = 1.3$ and luminosity $L_p = \epsilon_{\rm NT}\epsilon_{\rm dis}\dot{M}c^{2}$ in the inner accretion flow ($R=10R_{\rm g}$) of LLAGNs. Secondary meson/hadron ($pp$ and $p\gamma$ channels) cooling, decay, and particle transport are solved, and integrated over black hole mass functions and bolometric luminosity functions $\phi_{\rm bol}(L_{\rm bol})$ to compute the diffuse neutrino spectrum.
papers.reason: This paper investigates PeV diffuse neutrino background emission produced by magnetically arrested disks (MADs) in low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGNs), placing stringent constraints on the fraction of LLAGNs hosting MADs using IceCube data.

papers.title: Effects of Synchrotron Self-Absorption on Polarization Diagnostics of MHD Turbulence
papers.result:
SSA significantly suppresses polarized intensity and weakens spatial anisotropy while preserving the Kolmogorov power-law scaling $k^{-8/3}$ in the inertial range of the polarized power spectrum. The self-absorption turnover frequency scales as $
u_a \propto L^{0.30}$ and $
u_a \propto B^{1.30}$ (consistent with theoretical $
u_a \propto (\kappa B_\perp^{(p+2)/2} L)^{2/(p+4)}$), with total intensity reaching $I(
u) \propto 
u^{5/2}$ in the optically thick regime and $I(
u) \propto 
u^{-(p-1)/2} = 
u^{-0.85}$ in the optically thin regime. Furthermore, the variance-wavelength relation $P^2(\lambda^2)$ is modified in the presence of SSA: when $ ar{\phi} > \sigma_\phi$, the scaling shifts from $\lambda^{-2-2m+(p-1)}$ to $P^2 \propto \lambda^{-2-2m-5}$, preserving sensitivity to the magnetic turbulence spectral index $m$.
papers.problem: Prior statistical diagnostics of MHD turbulence using synchrotron polarization were strictly confined to the optically thin regime, failing to account for how synchrotron self-absorption affects polarization statistics, anisotropy, and depolarization in dense astrophysical plasmas.
papers.method:
Numerical integration of the full polarized radiative transfer equation for Stokes parameters $(I, Q, U, V)^T$ through $512^3$ isothermal 3D MHD turbulence simulations, including SSA coefficients $a_{I, Q} \propto (
u_{B\perp}/
u)^{\alpha+5/2}$, emission $j_{I, Q} \propto (
u_{B\perp}/
u)^\alpha$ with $\alpha=(p-1)/2$, and Faraday rotation $\mathrm{RM} = 0.812 \int (n_c/\mathrm{cm^{-3}})(B_\parallel/\mu\mathrm{G})(dl/\mathrm{pc})\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$.
papers.reason: The paper extends synchrotron polarization diagnostics of MHD turbulence into the synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) regime, directly relevant for modeling the polarized emission and Faraday effects in dense magnetized transient environments such as relativistic jets, supernova-CSM interactions, and compact radio sources.

papers.title: Far Ultraviolet Variability on Timescales of a Few hours in the Recurrent Nova M31N 2008-12a: Origin and Implications
papers.result: AstroSat/UVIT observations detect intrinsic FUV variability ($R > 4$) at $\sim 4.5\text{--}5.1\text{ days}$ post-eruption with a candidate modulation period of $P = 4.60^{+0.25}_{-0.15}\text{ hr}$ ($2.3\sigma$, $\mathrm{FAP} = 0.02$). The inferred Keplerian radius satisfies $r_{\mathrm{Kep}} < r_{\mathrm{circ}} < r_{\mathrm{RL}}$, ruling out fresh viscous re-accretion (which requires $t_{\mathrm{visc}} \sim 100\text{ days}$) and demonstrating accretion disk survival with low ejecta mass $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \sim 7.9 \times 10^{-8}\,M_{\odot}$.
papers.problem: Whether the accretion disk in rapidly recurring novae is completely destroyed by the thermonuclear runaway or can survive/rapidly re-establish, which dictates net mass growth toward the Chandrasekhar limit.
papers.method: Orbit-wise UVIT FUV PSF/aperture photometry quantified via excess variance $R = V/S = \left[\frac{1}{N-1}\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2\right] / \left[\frac{1}{N}\sum \sigma_i^2\right]$, weighted sine fitting, permutation tests, circularisation radius calculation $\frac{r_{\mathrm{circ}}}{a}=\left(1+\frac{M_{2}}{M_{1}}\right)\left(\frac{R_{L1}}{a}\right)^{4}$, and Cloudy photoionisation modelling.
papers.reason: The paper provides UV/X-ray observational evidence and timescale constraints for accretion disk survival in the rapid recurrent nova M31N 2008-12a, which directly addresses the central engine and mass accumulation of near-Chandrasekhar white dwarfs as Type Ia supernova progenitors.

papers.title: Magnetoelastic avalanches in magnetar crusts with plastic islands
papers.result: Dynamic crustal failure leads to collective avalanches and slow creeping failures that multiply the failed volume fraction by a factor of $\approx 4$ (from $f_{\rm fail}(0) \approx 9\%$ to $f_{\rm fail} = 35.4\%$ for global quakes, and $0.6\%$ to $2.6\%$ for localized quakes with $E_{\rm kin,0}=7.07\times 10^{41}\text{ erg}$). Avalanching develops promptly within $\approx 8\text{ ms}$, accompanied by discrete QPO modes (e.g., $18.79, 24.01, 49.52\text{ Hz}$, and localized high-frequency modes at $\sim 113.5\text{ Hz}$) that drift over beat timescales $T_{\rm beat} \sim |\omega_1 - \omega_2|^{-1} \sim 1\text{ s}$. The failure volume scales non-monotonically with the poloidal field $B_p$ peaking around $B_p \sim 10^{14}\text{ G}$, and scales with kick efficiency as $\frac{f_{\rm fail}(50\text{ ms})}{f_{\rm fail}(0)} = 3.7 + 0.193\ln\eta$.
papers.problem: Standard magnetar QPO models treat the crust as an elastic continuum that remains completely intact throughout oscillations, failing to account for dynamic yielding, plastic avalanching, and the resultant transient mode drifting observed in giant flare and burst tails.
papers.method: Linearized Einstein-Maxwell-Euler axial perturbations are solved in the time domain under the Cowling approximation ($\delta g_{\mu\nu} = 0$) using a central leapfrog scheme with CFL parameter $C_{\rm CFL}=0.25$ and local wave speed $v_{\mu B}=[(\mu+B^{2}/4\pi)/(\epsilon+p+B^{2}/4\pi)]^{1/2}$. Crustal yielding is monitored dynamically using the von Mises criterion with threshold $\sigma_{\rm yield}=\mu_{\rm eff}\varepsilon_{\max}$ ($\varepsilon_{\max}=0.1$); failed cells permanently drop their effective shear modulus to $\mu_{\rm eff}=0$, dissipating elastic strain while conserving hydrodynamic inertia.
papers.reason: This paper presents a relativistic 2D time-domain magnetoelastic simulation of magnetar crusts with dynamic failure ('plastic islands'), explaining the transient drift and cascading behavior of QPOs observed during magnetar bursts and giant flares.

papers.title: Finite-temperature ab-initio-Informed Nuclear Equation-of-State Tables (FINEST): Nuclear matter uncertainties in core-collapse supernovae
papers.result: Cold nuclear matter parameters introduce up to $\sim 150\text{ ms}$ delay in shock revival for high-compactness progenitors ($s24$, $\xi_{2.5}=0.44$), while very soft high-density matter ($P_{\rm SNM}=400\text{ MeV fm}^{-3}$) triggers black hole collapse within $500\text{ ms}$. Crucially, the thermal pressure is controlled by the nucleon effective mass $m^*$ via the thermal index $\Gamma_{\rm th} = 1 + P_{\rm th}/\epsilon_{\rm th} \approx \frac{5}{3} - \frac{n}{m^*}\frac{\partial m^*}{\partial n}$. A non-monotonic $m^*(n)$ functional ($m^*_{\rm HWS}$) reduces thermal pressure at densities exceeding saturation density $n_0$, accelerating protoneutron star (PNS) mantle contraction, which pushes neutrinospheres into hotter layers to enhance neutrino luminosity and successfully trigger delayed explosions, whereas standard monotonically decreasing Skyrme forms ($m^*_{\rm skyrme}$) fail to revive the shock and collapse into a black hole at $t_{\rm pb} \approx 1.65\text{ s}$.
papers.problem: Uncertainties in finite-temperature nuclear EOS tables—specifically the parameterizations of the in-medium nucleon effective mass $m^*(n)$ and high-density thermal pressure—remain poorly constrained by cold neutron star observations, leaving their direct impact on CCSN shock revival, neutrino-driven convection, and black hole formation ambiguous.
papers.method: Constructed finite-temperature, composition-dependent EOS tables using the HWS energy-density functional with baryonic kinetic energy $\epsilon_{\rm kin}(n,y,T) = \frac{1}{n}\left(\frac{\hbar^2\tau_n}{2m_n^*} + \frac{\hbar^2\tau_p}{2m_p^*}\right)$ and a single-nucleus approximation transitioning smoothly into nuclear statistical equilibrium (NSE with 3335 nuclides). Performed spherically symmetric radiation-hydrodynamic CCSN simulations using FLASH with M1 two-moment three-flavor neutrino transport and STIR turbulence-assisted convection (mixing-length parameter $\alpha_\Lambda = 1.25$) on $s20$ and $s24$ progenitor models.
papers.reason: This work introduces the FINEST finite-temperature equation of state (EOS) informed by ab initio chiral effective field theory and systematically quantifies how nuclear effective mass parameterizations affect core-collapse supernova (CCSN) central engine dynamics, neutrino heating, and fallback black hole formation.

papers.title: Core-Collapse Supernovae from Single and Binary-Stripped Massive Stars - I. Explodability and Nucleosynthesis
papers.result: Progenitors with $M_{\rm ZAMS} \le 22\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ explode reliably across both populations, yielding explosion energies $E_{\rm exp} \sim 0.4\text{--}1.3\times 10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ ($0.4\text{--}1.3\text{ B}$), baryonic remnant masses $M_{\rm rem} \sim 1.4\text{--}2.0\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, and explosion timescales $t_{\rm exp} \sim 0.30\text{--}0.65\text{ s}$. The Salpeter IMF-weighted Fe yield for binary-stripped models is $0.0589\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ (consistent with empirical observations of $0.058 \pm 0.007\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$), while single-star progenitors yield $0.0747\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$. Binary stripping enhances K yields by $\sim 3.4$ times ($\sim 0.63\text{ dex}$) and systematically improves agreement with galactic [S/Mg], [K/Mg], and [Ca/Mg] trends.
papers.problem: How binary interaction and envelope stripping modify the core compactness and pre-collapse progenitor structure of massive stars, and how these structural differences alter CCSN explodability, remnant properties, and nucleosynthetic yields across $M_{\rm ZAMS} = 11\text{--}45\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$.
papers.method: One-dimensional general-relativistic hydrodynamic simulations using the Agile-PUSH framework to trigger shock revival via extra heating $Q_{\rm push}^+(t, r)$ parameterized by the bounce compactness $\xi_{2.0} = 2.0 / [R(M=2.0\,{\rm M}_\odot)/1000\,{\rm km}]$ via $k_{\rm push} = a\xi_{2.0}^2 + b\xi_{2.0} + c$, coupled with large nuclear network post-processing (CFNET, 2902 isotopes) following thermodynamic trajectories with peak temperatures $T_{\rm peak} > 1.75\,{\rm GK}$.
papers.reason: This study provides a systematic comparison of explodability, remnant masses, and detailed nucleosynthetic yields between single-star and binary-stripped core-collapse supernova progenitors, directly constraining central engine energetics and ejecta composition.

papers.title: Identification of rippling interface between laser-ablated plasma and ambient uniform plasma at rest
papers.result: Using optical self-emission and collective Thomson scattering (CTS), the authors identify a rippling interface between the expanding laser-ablated Al piston and uniform N ambient plasma. Upstream parameters with $|B_{y0}| = 4\ \mathrm{T}$ yield an Alfvén speed $v_{\rm A} = |B_{y0}|/\sqrt{4\pi m_{\rm N}n_{\rm N}} \approx 92\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, which together with expansion velocity $V_{X^{\prime}} \approx 500\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ confirms a supercritical shock regime. CTS diagnoses electron density $n_e = (1.97\pm 0.26) \times 10^{18}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, $Z_{\rm Al} \approx 11$, and temperatures $T_e = 377\pm 19\ \mathrm{eV}$ and $T_i = 882\pm 16\ \mathrm{eV}$, confirming that the bright emission layer is dominated by piston Al plasma rather than compressed ambient plasma.
papers.problem: In laboratory experiments of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks, spatial inhomogeneity and boundary ambiguities make it difficult to determine whether detected reflected ions originate from the shock transition potential or the expanding piston-ambient plasma contact interface.
papers.method: The authors perform laser-driven plasma interaction experiments on the Gekko-XII facility under a uniform $1.0\ \mathrm{Torr}$ nitrogen background and external magnetic fields ($B_{y0} = \pm 4\ \mathrm{T}$), combined with 2D single-fluid ideal-MHD simulations using Athena++ modeling synthetic bremsstrahlung intensity $I_s \propto n_e n_s Z_s^2 T_s^{-1/2} e^{-h\nu / k_{\rm B} T_s} \propto \sqrt{\rho_s^5 / P_s}\, (Z_s^3 / A_s^{5/2}) \exp[-h\nu\rho_s / (P_s A_s)]$.
papers.reason: This laboratory astrophysics study clarifies the structure and dynamics of the contact interface in laser-driven magnetized collisionless shocks, offering insights into shock formation and particle reflection relevant to supernova remnants and circumstellar interactions.

papers.title: Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock
papers.result: The authors detect a foot-like structure and pronounced ion temperature anisotropy ($T_{i,\perp}/T_{i,\parallel} = T_{i,x}/T_{i,y} \lesssim 4.5$) upstream of the shock ramp in a supercritical collisionless shock with upstream parameters $v_A \approx 65\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, sound speed $a_s \approx 11\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $M_A > 3.8$, $M_s > 23$, $\beta_i \approx 0.02$, and $\beta_e \approx 0.06$. Linear kinetic dispersion analysis for foot plasma ($T_{i,\parallel} \sim 700\ \mathrm{eV}$, $T_{i,\perp} \sim 2300\ \mathrm{eV}$) demonstrates susceptibility to the Alfvén ion cyclotron (AIC) instability with growth rate $\gamma_{\max} = 0.31\,\omega_{ci}$ at $B=4\ \mathrm{T}$ (characteristic growth timescale $\tau \sim 20\ \mathrm{ns}$, wavelength $\lambda_{\max} \sim 4\ \mathrm{mm}$).
papers.problem: In supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks, anomalous resistivity alone is insufficient to support the required energy dissipation; identifying laboratory experimental evidence for upstream ion reflection and associated kinetic temperature anisotropy has remained challenging.
papers.method: Laser-driven shock experiment using the Gekko-XII HIPER facility ablating an Al target into an ambient nitrogen gas ($P_{\rm N} = 1.5, 2.0\ \mathrm{Torr}$) immersed in a perpendicular magnetic field $B_{y0} \approx -4\ \mathrm{T}$, diagnosed via Gated Optical Imager (GOI), Streaked Optical Pyrometer (SOP), two-channel collective Thomson scattering (CTS) targeting the ion acoustic wave (IAW) and electron plasma wave (EPW) features, combined with 1D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations and linear Vlasov kinetic dispersion theory.
papers.reason: The paper provides direct laboratory astrophysics evidence for reflected ions and ion temperature anisotropy in a forming supercritical magnetized collisionless shock ($M_A > 3.8$), which directly connects to microphysical shock dissipation and particle acceleration models in supernova remnants and shock breakout environments.

papers.title: A MAGNHIFFIC cold-gas filament fuelling the nuclear activity of NGC 3100
papers.result: The authors detect a $\sim 340\ \mathrm{kpc}$ stellar-free $\mathrm{H\,I}$ filament with mass $M_{\mathrm{HI}} = 3.4 \times 10^8\ M_\odot$ feeding the circum-nuclear disc of early-type galaxy NGC 3100 ($D = 38\ \mathrm{Mpc}$). High-velocity-resolution absorption against the core reveals redshifted infalling cold gas clouds with column density $N_{\mathrm{HI}} = 63 \times 10^{16}\,(T_{\mathrm{spin}}/c_f)\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ and mass $M_{\mathrm{HI}} \sim 2.4 \times 10^4\ M_\odot$, coexisting with jet-driven molecular gas outflows of mass $M_{\mathrm{out}} = 5.6 \times 10^4\ M_\odot$ and outflow rate $\dot{M}_{\mathrm{out}} \lesssim 0.12\ M_\odot\ \mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ driven by a low-power jet ($P_{1.4\ \mathrm{GHz}} = 1 \times 10^{23}\ \mathrm{W\ Hz^{-1}}$).
papers.problem: Tracing how cold diffuse neutral gas fuels active galactic nuclei (AGN) across scales from circum-galactic environments ($>100\ \mathrm{kpc}$) to sub-kpc circum-nuclear discs, and verifying whether simultaneous chaotic cold accretion and low-power jet-ISM feedback operate in early-type galaxies.
papers.method: Deep 25-hour MeerKAT 21-cm line interferometry combined with CARACal calibration pipeline (achieving column density sensitivity $N_{\rm HI}^{3\sigma, 10\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}} = 0.29 \times 10^{19}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$), multi-Gaussian absorption decomposition, VST optical deep imaging, and ALMA $^{12}\mathrm{CO}(1-0)$, $(2-1)$, and $(3-2)$ line kinematic and ratio ($R_{21} = T_{\mathrm{CO}(2-1)} / T_{\mathrm{CO}(1-0)}$) analysis.
papers.reason: This paper presents ultra-deep MeerKAT 21-cm and ALMA CO observations mapping cold gas accretion and multi-phase jet-ISM interaction in NGC 3100 down to sub-kpc scales. It provides an empirical case study of relativistic jet feedback, circum-nuclear fueling, and chaotic cold accretion in low-power radio galaxies.

papers.title: Probing In-Medium Neutron-to-Dark-Fermion Conversion with Multimessenger Neutron Star Observations
papers.result: In-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion softens the nuclear EOS by reducing neutron fraction $Y_n$ and increasing dark fermion abundance $Y_\chi = n_\chi / n_B$. Weakly repulsive regimes ($G_\chi = 1$--$11~\mathrm{fm}^2$, $m_\chi = 939$--$1300~\mathrm{MeV}$) fail to support $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$ and are ruled out across the nuclear EOS ensemble. In the Illinois-Maryland analysis, the active conservative boundary is driven by $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$, while strict X-PSI/Amsterdam tests yield no common parameter point satisfying all 13 baseline EOSs, with the maximum compatibility ($N_{\rm cons} = 11$) confined to $m_\chi = 939$--$950~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $G_\chi = 19$--$21~\mathrm{fm}^2$.
papers.problem: Whether in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion ($n \to \chi$), occurring when the neutron chemical potential exceeds the dark fermion mass ($\mu_n \ge m_\chi$), can survive multi-messenger astrophysical constraints from maximum neutron star masses ($M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$), GW170817 tidal deformabilities ($70 \le \Lambda_{1.4} \le 580$), and NICER mass-radius determinations across diverse nuclear EOSs.
papers.method: A non-linear $\sigma$--$\omega$--$\rho$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) model is employed across an ensemble of 21 unified nucleonic EOSs. In dense matter, chemical equilibrium $\mu_\chi = \mu_n$ is solved self-consistently with $\beta$-equilibrium and charge neutrality, where the dark sector includes vector-meson-mediated repulsive self-interactions giving $\mu_\chi = \sqrt{k_{F,\chi}^2 + m_\chi^2} + G_\chi n_\chi$ with effective coupling $G_\chi \equiv (g_V / m_V)^2$ and energy density contribution $\varepsilon_{\chi\text{-int}} = \frac{1}{2} G_\chi n_\chi^2$.
papers.reason: This paper investigates in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion in dense neutron star cores using multimessenger constraints (maximum mass $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$, GW170817 tidal deformability, and NICER mass-radius measurements). It offers valuable insights into neutron star interior physics and equation of state softening under exotic degree-of-freedom transitions.

papers.title: Contributions of massive stars and classical novae to Galactic 26Al
papers.result: Fitting the radial 1.809 MeV emission across Galactocentric annuli reveals that classical novae dominate Galactic $^{26}\mathrm{Al}$ with a baseline contribution of $77^{+14}_{-15}\%$, while massive stars account for only $23^{+13}_{-14}\%$. A massive star fraction of $\sim 23\%$ yields a revised Galactic star formation rate of $\mathrm{SFR} = 1.2\text{--}1.8\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and increases the massive-star/core-collapse supernova $^{60}\mathrm{Fe}/^{26}\mathrm{Al}$ yield ratio to $0.8 \pm 0.2$, matching theoretical predictions.
papers.problem: Pure massive star and core-collapse supernova models for Galactic $^{26}\mathrm{Al}$ yield an overly high star formation rate ($\gtrsim 5\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$) compared to independent estimates ($1\text{--}2\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$) and severely underestimate the observed $^{60}\mathrm{Fe}/^{26}\mathrm{Al}$ gamma-ray flux ratio ($0.182 \pm 0.042$).
papers.method: The authors analyze 20.5 years (305 Ms) of INTEGRAL/SPI data around $1.809\,\mathrm{MeV}$ using forward-fitting of instrumental background and spatial source templates across Galactocentric radial rings (0–2, 2–4, 4–6, 6–8, 8–10, 10–15 kpc), fitting the radial mass profiles with linear combinations $M(a_{\text{N}}, a_{\text{MS}}) = a_{\text{N}} M_{\text{N}} + a_{\text{MS}} M_{\text{MS}}$ against Galactic chemical evolution predictions.
papers.reason: The paper uses 20.5 years of INTEGRAL/SPI gamma-ray observations to decompose the origin of Galactic 26Al, showing classical novae likely contribute 77% while massive stars contribute 23%, directly resolving longstanding tensions in the Galactic star formation rate and 60Fe/26Al yield ratios from core-collapse supernovae.

papers.title: ePNGCAT: the first eROSITA all-sky data release
papers.result: The catalogue contains 63,260 sources over 99.54% of the sky with an estimated 50% completeness limit of $3.12 \times 10^{-13}\ \mathrm{erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ in the $0.2$--$2.3\ \mathrm{keV}$ band, a median positional offset of $72''$, and an overall multiplicative broad-band flux dispersion of $26.5\%$ relative to eRASS1.
papers.problem: Public access to the first eROSITA all-sky survey (eRASS1) is restricted to the western Galactic hemisphere, leaving the eastern half proprietary without an official public point-source catalogue.
papers.method: Sources were extracted by nonlinearly inverting the 8-bit RGB image via an empirical inverse hyperbolic sine mapping $I_c = \sinh((\nu_c - \nu_0)/A_c)$, matched-filter filtering with a $\mathrm{S/N} = 3.5$ detection threshold, radial sigmoid PSF fitting for 2,759 saturated bright cores, and flux/position calibration using HistGradientBoostingRegressor trained on western eRASS1 data.
papers.reason: The paper constructs ePNGCAT, an all-sky X-ray catalogue of 63,260 sources derived from the public eROSITA eRASS1 RGB PNG image, recovering ~10,800 real X-ray sources in the proprietary eastern hemisphere with ~1' positional accuracy.

papers.title: Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
papers.result: Ab initio chiral effective field theory predictions determine neutron-skin thicknesses $R_{\mathrm{skin}}(^{48}\mathrm{Ca}) = 0.120(14)(12)\ \mathrm{fm}$ and $R_{\mathrm{skin}}(^{208}\mathrm{Pb}) = 0.187(25)(18)\ \mathrm{fm}$, favoring a soft-to-moderate symmetry energy slope $38.3 \le L \le 68.5\ \mathrm{MeV}$ and $J \sim 30\text{--}32\ \mathrm{MeV}$ consistent with GW170817 and NICER astrophysical constraints, while isoscalar giant monopole resonance (ISGMR) data constrain symmetric nuclear matter incompressibility to $K_0 \sim 190\text{--}240\ \mathrm{MeV}$.
papers.problem: Tensions in constraining the nuclear symmetry energy slope $L$ and neutron-skin thickness $R_{\mathrm{skin}}$, particularly reconciling the stiff EOS inferred from PREX-II parity-violating electron scattering with softer constraints from CREX, electric dipole polarizability $\alpha_D$, and astrophysical neutron star measurements.
papers.method: Microscopic ab initio many-body nuclear frameworks (e.g., chiral EFT, coupled-cluster with Lorentz integral transform, IMSRG) applied to finite-nucleus observables: dipole polarizability $\alpha_D = 2\alpha \int_0^\infty d\omega \frac{R(\omega)}{\omega}$, skin thickness $R_{\mathrm{skin}} = R_n - R_p$, and ISGMR incompressibility scaling $K_A = \frac{M}{\hbar^2} \langle R_m^2 \rangle E_{\mathrm{ISGMR}}^2 = K_{\mathrm{vol}} + K_{\mathrm{surf}}A^{-1/3} + K_{\mathrm{Coul}}Z^2 A^{-4/3} + K_\tau \frac{(N-Z)^2}{A^2}$ to map microphysics to TOV hydrostatic equilibria.
papers.reason: This review provides an ab initio nuclear theory perspective on nuclear matter equation of state (EOS) parameters ($J$, $L$, and $K_0$) that govern neutron star structure, radii, and tidal deformabilities relevant to transient astrophysical compact object engines and GW170817/NICER constraints.

papers.title: Resolving a Clumpy Disk Wind in 4U 1957+115 with XRISM
papers.result: The observation detects Fe XXVI and Fe XXV absorption lines with confidence up to $5.6\sigma$ during orbital phase $\phi \sim 0$, revealing an outflow velocity $v_{\rm out} = 140_{-20}^{+30}~{\rm km/s}$ and an intrinsic turbulence limit $v_{\rm turb} \lesssim 70~{\rm km/s}$ (narrowed down from $v_{\rm turb} = 350_{-170}^{+290}~{\rm km/s}$ in time-averaged spectra). Photoionization modeling with pion yields $\log \xi = 5.8_{-0.5}^{+0.3}$ and $N_{\rm H,PION} = 4.8_{-3.7}^{+1.7} \times 10^{23}~{\rm cm^{-2}}$, placing the maximum wind launching radius at $r_{\rm max} = L_{\rm ion}/(\xi N_{\rm H}) \sim 10^8 - 10^{10} (d_{10})^2~{\rm cm}$, far inside the Compton radius $R_{\rm IC} = (5 \pm 1) \times 10^{11}~{\rm cm}$ and below the local escape velocity.
papers.problem: Investigating whether persistent black hole candidate 4U 1957+115 launches an intrinsic disk wind, resolving whether line broadening is caused by true microscopic turbulence or time-averaged bulk motion, and determining the physical driving mechanism and geometry of the absorbing medium.
papers.method: XRISM/Resolve high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy (62 ks effective exposure) modeled with continuous continuum components `TBabs(diskbb+powerlaw)`, Gaussian line-search scans (step size 2 eV, width 50–1000 km/s), relativistic reflection tests (`relxilllp`), and self-consistent photoionization modeling with `pion` across time segments (Part 1 vs. Part 2) and binary orbital phases.
papers.reason: This paper presents the first high-resolution XRISM/Resolve spectroscopic detection of an intrinsic, clumpy accretion disk wind in the persistent black hole candidate 4U 1957+115, providing direct constraints on outflow kinematics and driving mechanisms relevant to compact object accretion physics.

papers.title: Analytical modeling of the gamma-ray morphology of TeV halos around moving pulsars
papers.result: The authors derive a closed-form analytical approximation for the projected line-of-sight (LOS) electron surface density $\Sigma(\rho,\phi,E) = \mathcal{S}(E)\mathcal{T}(\rho,\phi,E)$ around a moving pulsar. In the far-field limit $\rho, v\tau, r_d \ll d$, the 3D diffusion-loss convolution reduces to a single integral over injection history, and upon spatial integration $\int_0^{2\pi}d\phi\int_0^\infty \rho d\rho\,\Sigma$, the dependence on diffusion coefficient $D(E)$ and pulsar velocity $v$ strictly cancels, yielding an equilibrium lepton spectrum $N_{\rm eq}(E) \simeq q(E)\tau_{\max}(E)$.
papers.problem: Pulsar proper motion ($v_{\rm psr} \sim 100\text{--}500\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) displaces the injection center over the cooling time $\tau_{\rm loss}(E)$, creating asymmetric, elongated TeV halo morphologies along the trajectory. Existing approaches require computationally prohibitive multi-dimensional numerical convolutions over LOS and injection history, hindering fast parameter inference and morphological fits to observational data from HAWC and LHAASO.
papers.method: The framework models uniform pulsar motion $\mathbf{x}_{s}(t) = \mathbf{x}_{\rm age} + \mathbf{v}(t - t_{\rm age})$ with isotropic diffusion coefficient $D(E)$ and continuous injection $q(E, t)$. By completing the square along the LOS coordinate $\mathbf{x}_{\rm los} = \mathbf{x}_{\rm obs} + s\mathbf{n}$, the exact LOS integral is expressed in terms of the complementary error function $\mathrm{erfc}(a_n/r_d)$. In the far-field approximation, the spatial separation simplifies to $a^2 - a_n^2 \simeq \rho^2 + (v\tau)^2 + 2\rho v\tau\cos\phi$, and introducing the dimensionless parameters $\chi = \tau/\tau_D$, $\eta = \tau_v/\tau_D = 4D(E)/(\rho v)$ allows closed-form integration using modified Bessel functions $K_0$ and error functions $\mathrm{erf}$.
papers.reason: This work develops an analytical modeling framework for the gamma-ray morphology of TeV halos around moving pulsars, directly relevant to high-energy observations of compact objects and leptonic cosmic-ray transport.

papers.title: Binary Progenitors of Electron-capture Supernovae
papers.result: In surviving binaries, stripping produces predominantly Type Ib ($\sim 60\%$), Type II ($\sim 30\%$), and Type IIb ($\sim 10\%$) events, while Type Ic is $< 0.4\%$. Accretion spin-up yields near-critical companion rotation ($\omega/\omega_{\rm crit} \ge 0.8$) concentrated at $P_{\rm orb,postSN} \sim 10-100\ \mathrm{d}$ and $e \simeq 0.1-0.3$, matching BeXRB precursors, with a local cosmic ECSN rate density of $(4-7) \times 10^3\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ representing $f_{\rm ECSN} \approx 1\%-4\%$ of core-collapse events.
papers.problem: The parameter space, envelope stripping outcomes, progenitor spectral classifications, and cosmic rates of electron-capture supernovae across metallicities remain uncertain due to complex binary interactions.
papers.method: Using the POSYDON binary population synthesis framework across metallicities from $Z/Z_\odot = 2$ to $10^{-4}$, systems are classified as ECSN progenitors when the carbon-oxygen core mass at carbon depletion falls within $1.37 M_\odot \leq M_{\rm CO} \leq 1.43 M_\odot$, adopting an intrinsic natal kick dispersion of $\sigma = 20\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$.
papers.reason: This work models the binary evolution and envelope stripping pathways of electron-capture supernova (ECSN) progenitors, placing critical constraints on compact object formation engines and natal kicks.

papers.title: Gaia DR3 Compact Binary Candidates Constrained by Radial Velocity Measurements
papers.result: Among the 518 binaries with effective radial velocity epochs $n_{\mathrm{eff}} \ge 3$, 192 are classified as Good-fit sources, containing 171 Medium-priority or higher compact binary candidates; this includes 4 candidates with fitted secondary mass $M_{2,\mathrm{fit}} > 2.1\,M_\odot$ (including a Critical candidate with $M_{2,\mathrm{fit}} \sim 2.3\,M_\odot$ and companions up to $\sim 3.2\,M_\odot$), 22 sources with $1.4\,M_\odot \le M_{2,\mathrm{fit}} \le 2.1\,M_\odot$, and 145 sources with $M_{2,\mathrm{fit}} < 1.4\,M_\odot$.
papers.problem: Identifying dormant compact object companions (neutron stars and black holes) in astrometric binaries and validating their orbital parameters against potential spurious solutions using multi-epoch radial velocity constraints.
papers.method: Performed joint MCMC orbital fitting combining Gaia astrometric orbital likelihoods with ground-based radial velocity data (accounting for zero-point offsets) using `emcee`, screening reliable solutions via goodness-of-fit thresholds $\chi^2 \le 10$, median normalized residual $z \le 2$, and $2\sigma$ epoch fraction $f_{2\sigma} \ge 0.6$.
papers.reason: The study provides systematic joint Gaia DR3 astrometry and multi-epoch ground-based radial velocity fitting to discover and characterize dormant compact binary candidates (neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes).

papers.title: A frequency-resolved measurement of the scattering law in FRB 20210415C
papers.result:
Across 8 sub-bands spanning $400.2	ext{--}765.6~\mathrm{MHz}$, the scattering index is measured to be $\alpha = -3.95 \pm 0.07$ (free Gaussian width) and $\alpha = -4.14 \pm 0.08$ (fixed Gaussian width), with a 34-parameter joint MCMC yielding $\alpha = -3.95 \pm 0.06$ and $	au_{m ref} = 7.97 \pm 0.09~\mathrm{ms}$ at $
u_{m ref} = 583~\mathrm{MHz}$ (corresponding to $	au_{m s} \simeq 7.0	ext{--}7.1~\mathrm{ms}$ at $600~\mathrm{MHz}$). The intrinsic pulse width exhibits frequency narrowing with $\sigma_{m int} \propto 
u^{ eta}$ ($ eta = -0.92 \pm 0.19$ for $
u > 440~\mathrm{MHz}$), with low-frequency excess width ($\,4.8\sigma\,$ at $\sim 422~\mathrm{MHz}$) favoring a thick-screen scattering medium.
papers.problem: Investigating whether the prominent asymmetric temporal tail in FRB 20210415C originates from multi-path plasma scattering following the theoretical power-law $\tau_{\rm s}(\nu) \propto \nu^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha \simeq -4$ or from intrinsic emission mechanisms.
papers.method:
Sub-band time profiles across $400.2	ext{--}765.6~\mathrm{MHz}$ were constructed using flux-weighted effective frequencies $
u_{{m eff},j} = \sum S_i 
u_i / \sum S_i$ and fitted with exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) models $I(t) = A [G(t; \mu, \sigma_{m int}) * E(t; 	au_{m emp})] + C$; power-law parameters $	au_{m emp}(
u) = 	au_{m ref} (

u_{m ref})^\alpha$ were determined through non-linear least squares and joint 34-parameter MCMC fitting, along with spectral autocorrelation function (ACF) searches for scintillation.
papers.reason: The paper provides a rigorous frequency-resolved test of the multi-path scattering law in the repeating FRB 20210219C (burst FRB 20210415C), verifying consistency with the canonical $\nu^{-4}$ scattering law against intrinsic asymmetry models.

papers.title: Comparison of Hybrid and Standard Reconstruction Methods on IXPE Astrophysical Data
papers.result: In the accreting X-ray pulsar Her X-1, the hybrid method increases polarimetric significance above $2.83\;\mathrm{keV}$, reaching a significance ratio $R = \sigma_{\mathrm{hyb}}/\sigma_{\mathrm{std}} = 1.180 \pm 0.029$ ($6.2\sigma$ above unity) at $5.66\text{--}8.00\;\mathrm{keV}$, which corresponds to an equivalent effective area increase of $\Delta A_{\mathrm{eff}}/A_{\mathrm{eff}} = R^2 - 1 = 39.3\% \pm 6.8\%$. In the unpolarized source XTE J1701-461, no spurious polarization is induced ($R \le 1.7\sigma$ from 1 across all bands).
papers.problem: The hybrid reconstruction method combines convolutional neural networks (CNN) with standard moment analysis but had only been calibrated using monochromatic laboratory beams; its sensitivity gains, potential systematic biases, and pixel geometry artifacts required observational verification on broad-band astrophysical X-ray sources.
papers.method: Reconstructed IXPE Level 1 events by coupling CNN-predicted photon impact points with dedicated modulation factor curves across 4 logarithmic energy bands in $2.00\text{--}8.00\;\mathrm{keV}$; quantified performance via the significance ratio $R = \sigma_{\mathrm{hyb}}/\sigma_{\mathrm{std}} \equiv R_{\mathrm{PD}} R_{\mathrm{err}}$ incorporating photon-level covariance ($\rho \approx 0.999$), equivalent effective area change $\Delta A_{\mathrm{eff}}/A_{\mathrm{eff}} = R^2 - 1$, and Fourier harmonic analysis of the photoelectron angle distribution.
papers.reason: This work validates the deep learning-based hybrid track reconstruction algorithm on actual IXPE polarization observations of compact objects (Her X-1 and XTE J1701-461), proving sensitivity gains and characterizing detector systematics.

papers.title: Torque lags from magnetic unlocking in neutron stars and gravitational-wave smearing
papers.result:
Magnetic unlocking produces differential rotation with lag $\Delta
u \sim -	au_{m eff}\dot{
u}_{m R}$ between the core toroidal region and the crust, separating quadrupoles $\epsilon_{m pol}$ and $\epsilon_{m tor}$ into a distinct or smeared spectrum. The resulting continuous GW signal spans $\Delta f_{m GW} \approx 2\Delta
u$, diluting the coherent Fourier strain amplitude per bin by $|	ilde{h}_{m bin}|/|	ilde{h}_{m line}| \sim (\Delta f_{m GW}T)^{-1}$ and degrading the detection sensitivity by a factor of $(\Delta f_{m GW}T)^{1/2}$ for semicoherent searches when $\Delta f_{m GW}T \gg 1$.
papers.problem: Continuous gravitational-wave searches from neutron stars assume that mass quadrupoles phase-lock to the crustal rotation ($f = 2\nu_{\rm R}$), which may cause observers to miss signals if magnetic decoupling creates differential rotation and spreads the quadrupole radiation across frequencies.
papers.method:
The authors model continuous GW emission by decomposing the density into rigid ($ho_{m R}$) and differentially rotating ($ho_\Delta$) components, formulating the strain via a quadrupole-weighted pattern speed distribution $	ilde{h}_{ij}^{\Delta}(f) = - rac{64\pi^2 G T}{c^4 d}\int d
u_Q\,
u_Q^2 W_{ij}(
u_Q)\operatorname{sinc}[2T(f-2
u_Q)]$. They then evaluate effective torque lag coupling timescales $	au_{m eff}^{-1} \simeq 	au_B^{-1} + 	au_{\eta,\perp}^{-1} + 	au_\kappa^{-1} + [	au_{m ES}^{( eta)}]^{-1} + 	au_{m mf}^{-1}$ including composition-controlled Eddington-Sweet, transverse viscous, and Ekman processes.
papers.reason: The paper demonstrates how magnetic unlocking in neutron stars decouples toroidal magnetic regions from crustal spin-down torques, shifting and smearing the continuous gravitational-wave spectrum across a bandwidth $\Delta f_{\rm GW} \approx 2\Delta\nu$. This provides a theoretical mechanism explaining why monochromatic targeted/narrowband GW searches may systematically miss highly deformed magnetars or pulsars.

papers.title: $Δ(1232)$ isobars and neutrino opacities in hot dense matter
papers.result: When the threshold condition $\mu_n + \mu_e > M_{\Delta^-}^* + U_{\Delta^-}$ is met, the three-body absorption reaction $\bar{\nu}_e + e^- + n \to \Delta^-$ dominates the opacity, suppressing the antineutrino Rosseland mean free path $\lambda_R$ from $3\text{--}300\text{ m}$ down to $0.5\text{--}16\text{ cm}$ (a reduction factor of $83$ to $4.5\times 10^4$) at densities of $2\text{--}4n_0$. For electron neutrinos, $\lambda_R$ is shortened by factors of $1.7\text{--}6.5$ (for $Y_L=0.2\text{--}0.3$) and up to $4\text{--}200$ (for $Y_L=0.1$, following $\lambda_R^N/\lambda_R^{N\Delta} \approx \exp(a Y_\Delta)$). Consequently, the antineutrino share of the lepton-number diffusion coefficient $D_2$ drops from up to $69\%$ to below $7\%$, reducing total lepton diffusion by up to a factor of 3 at $Y_L=0.1$, while total energy diffusion $D_4$ changes by $<2\%$.
papers.problem: Neutrino transport in proto-neutron stars and neutron star mergers determines cooling, deleptonization timescales, and nucleosynthetic yields, but previous opacity calculations routinely omitted $\Delta(1232)$ isobars or neglected kinematically unsuppressed multi-body absorption channels like $\bar{\nu}_e + e^- + n \to \Delta^-$.
papers.method: Evaluated two-body charged/neutral-current scattering and three-body absorption $\bar{\nu}_e + e^- + n \to \Delta^-$ opacities using RMF kinematics (DDME2 and QMC-RMF3 models) with $N\Delta$ weak transition form factors under Rarita-Schwinger spin-3/2 projection; applied collision broadening via energy convolution $S_\Gamma(q_0)$ with detailed balance $S(-q_0) = e^{-q_0/T}S(q_0)$ and RPA static corrections via thermodynamic susceptibilities $\chi_{ij} = \partial n_i / \partial \mu_j |_T$.
papers.reason: The paper provides microscopic calculations of neutrino opacities in hot, dense matter with Delta(1232) isobars relevant to proto-neutron stars and merger remnants, demonstrating that three-body antineutrino absorption drastically shortens the antineutrino mean free path to centimeters.

papers.title: The biases caused by interpolated table models and their impact on X-ray spectroscopy
papers.result: Linear interpolation of non-linear models introduces a single-parameter error $e(\theta) = m(\theta) - \tilde{m}(\theta) = -\frac{1}{2} m''(\xi)(\theta - \theta_i)(\theta_{i+1} - \theta)$, which distorts the log-likelihood by adding a quadratic penalty $-\frac{1}{2} \sum_k \frac{e_k^2(\theta)}{\sigma_k^2}$ and a residual cross-term $-\sum_k \frac{e_k(\theta)[d_k - m_k(\theta)]}{\sigma_k^2}$. Its first derivative $\frac{d \ln \tilde{\mathcal{L}}}{d \theta} = \frac{d \ln \mathcal{L}}{d \theta} - \sum_k \frac{e_k e'_k - e_k m'_k + e'_k (d_k - m_k)}{\sigma_k^2}$ introduces discontinuous jumps at grid points via $e'_k(d_k - m_k)$, generating artificial modes. In real NuSTAR fits of MAXI J1820+070, table models induced artificial multimodality (e.g., spin $a$, photon index $\Gamma = 1.6$), causing affine-invariant MCMC acceptance rates to drop to $\approx 5\%$ and autocorrelation times to blow up to $\tau \approx 4000\text{--}16000$.
papers.problem: Investigating how linear interpolation errors in pre-computed X-ray spectral grid models distort the underlying likelihood landscape, bias Bayesian parameter recovery, and degrade MCMC/gradient-based optimization performance.
papers.method: Analytical Taylor-series derivation of interpolation errors and likelihood distortions in 1D and $n$-dimensions ($e(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = -\frac{1}{2} \sum_j H_{j,j}(\theta_j - \theta_{j,i})(\theta_{j,i+1} - \theta_j)$), combined with synthetic spectra tests and real NuSTAR observations of the BHXRB MAXI J1820+070 in the SIMS and hard states comparing Affine-Invariant Ensemble MCMC and dynamic nested sampling (Dynesty).
papers.reason: The paper demonstrates that linear interpolation in pre-computed X-ray table models (e.g., Relxill, kerrbb) introduces severe likelihood distortions, parameter biases, and artificial multimodality in Bayesian and gradient-based spectral fitting. This directly impacts parameter inference and reflection modeling for compact objects and relativistic transients.

papers.title: Investigating supernova-remnant X-ray maps with dendrogram-based techniques
papers.result: The dendrogram and GNN embedding analyses reveal distinct elemental spatial co-locations (e.g. $\mathrm{Si}$ with $\mathrm{S}$, $\mathrm{Ar}$ with $\mathrm{Ca}$, and $\mathrm{Fe\;XXV}$ with $\mathrm{Ni\;XXVI}$) and demonstrate that W49B clusters closer to core-collapse (CC) SNRs (Cas A, G292.0+1.8) than to Type Ia SNRs (Tycho, Kepler). Computing runtime scales from $15937.0\;\mathrm{ms}$ for GNN and $16962.7\;\mathrm{ms}$ for cosine-distance HC to $1365064.8\;\mathrm{ms}$ for bootstrap-validated SVHC over a 50-band dataset.

papers.title: Revisiting supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons
papers.result: Using the SFHo-18.8 ($18.8\,M_\odot$) core profile, the SN1987A cooling bounds exclude gauge boson masses up to $m_{A'} \lesssim 230\text{ MeV}$, $m_{Z'} \lesssim 280\text{ MeV}$ ($B-L$), and $m_{Z'} \lesssim 300\text{ MeV}$ ($L_\mu-L_\tau$). LESN mantle deposition limits constrain couplings down to $\epsilon \gtrsim 5.8 \times 10^{-12}$ for dark photons ($m_{A'} \le 450\text{ MeV}$), $g_{BL} \gtrsim 1.9 \times 10^{-12}$ for $U(1)_{B-L}$ ($m_{Z'} \le 440\text{ MeV}$), and $g_{\mu\tau} \gtrsim 6.4 \times 10^{-12}$ for $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ ($m_{Z'} \le 600\text{ MeV}$), scaling in the optically thin limit as $E_{\rm dep}^{(A')} \propto \epsilon^2$ and $E_{\rm dep}^{(Z')} \propto g_{BL}^4$.
papers.problem: Previous supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons often relied on soft-radiation approximations or simplified profiles, failing to capture detailed nucleon recoil $\mathcal{O}(\mathbf{k}^2/m_N^2)$, in-medium plasma modifications, and precise radial profiles of absorption and decay in the stellar mantle.
papers.method: Evaluated one-pion exchange (OPE) nucleon bremsstrahlung ($N+N \to N+N+Z'$) retaining non-relativistic momentum corrections $\mathcal{O}(\mathbf{k}^2/m_N^2)$ and in-medium effective mixing $\tilde{g}_p^{T,L} = g_p m_{Z'}^2 / (m_{Z'}^2 - \operatorname{Re}\Pi_{\gamma\gamma}^{T,L} - i\operatorname{Im}\Pi_{\gamma\gamma}^{T,L})$, applied the Raffelt cooling criterion $\mathcal{L}_{\rm BSM} < 3\times 10^{52}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$, and tracked geometric optical depth $\tau(r)$ and mantle energy deposition $E_{\rm dep} = \Delta t (\mathcal{P}_{\rm c} - \mathcal{P}_{\rm m}) < E_{\rm exp} \sim 10^{50}\text{ erg}$.
papers.reason: This paper provides a rigorous revision of supernova cooling (SN1987A) and low-energy supernova (LESN) energy-deposition bounds on dark photons and dark gauge bosons ($U(1)_{B-L}$ and $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$), incorporating finite-momentum nucleon bremsstrahlung and self-consistent medium effects relevant to core-collapse supernova physics.

papers.title: Classification of Fermi Blazars of Uncertain Type Using Positive-Unlabelled Machine Learning
papers.result: Out of 1623 Fermi 4FGL-DR4 BCUs, the PU ensemble classifies 437 sources as FSRQ-like candidates, 597 as BL Lac-like candidates, flags 12 sources as ambiguous candidates meeting both criteria, and leaves 577 sources unclassified. The BCU FSRQ candidates exhibit a softer median photon index of $\Gamma = 2.60$ compared to known FSRQs ($\Gamma = 2.47$), while unclassified BCUs are systematically fainter (median $\log F_{1000} = -9.77$) with $25.3\%$ located in the Galactic plane ($|b| < 10^\circ$).

papers.method: An ensemble of five PU classifiers (CE, WE, Bagging PU, MLR, and PU Extra Trees with $\hat{R}_{\mathrm{uPU}}/\hat{R}_{\mathrm{nnPU}}$ estimators) is constructed under the Selected Completely At Random (SCAR) assumption $P(s=1\mid y=1,\mathbf{x}) = c$, evaluating seven Fermi $\gamma$-ray features (`PL_Index`, `LP_beta`, `LP_SigCurv`, `log_Pivot_Energy`, `log_Flux1000`, `log_Variability_Index`, `log_Flux_Peak`) separately in FSRQ mode and BL Lac mode.

papers.title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
papers.result: In the late inspiral stage ($D = 2.5 R_*$), nonlinear tidal interactions reduce the neutron star quadrupole fundamental mode ($f$-mode) frequency by $\sim 10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and impart an extra gravitational-wave phase shift of $\Delta \Phi_X \sim \mathcal{O}(1)\ \mathrm{rad}$ beyond the linear tidal response up to $f_{\rm GW} = 1100\ \mathrm{Hz}$. The second-order perturbative frequency shift scales as $\Delta f^{(2)} \propto q^2$ (where $q = M_c / M_*$), and the radial mode frequency drops by $8.8\%$ to $f_r = 0.3173$ due to nonlinear $c_{20}$–$c_r$ coupling.
papers.problem: Linear tidal theory assumes that external tidal driving forces a response without shifting stellar eigenfrequencies, breaking down during late binary inspirals where strong nonlinear mode couplings alter the restoring forces and induce unmodeled phase errors in gravitational-wave templates.
papers.method: Solves the complete 3D Newtonian nonlinear Euler-Poisson equations for non-rotating $\Gamma=2$ polytropes using Athena++ under a time-varying quadrupolar tidal potential $U_{\rm tide}(\bm{x}, t)$, coupled with an analytical multi-mode coupling model incorporating $l=0$ radial and $l=2, 4$ $f$-modes via three-mode and four-mode coupling coefficients ($\kappa_{abc}$, $\zeta_{abcd}$), and incorporates Burke-Thorne radiation reaction terms $a_i^{\rm BT}$ to trace self-consistent orbital and phase evolution.
papers.reason: The paper presents full nonlinear hydrodynamical simulations and an analytical mode-coupling framework for binary neutron star late inspirals, quantifying nonlinear tidal frequency shifts and gravitational-wave phase shifts relevant to compact object mergers.

papers.title: The long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus: a comparison between GRMHD simulations and relativistic thin disk theory
papers.result: The long-term evolution of the bound accretion disk and mass accretion rate follows power-law decay behaviors: $\dot{M}(t) \propto t^{-n}$ with $n=(4-2\mu)/(3-2\mu)$, outer disk radius $r_{\rm out} \sim \sigma_{\rm eff}(t) \sim t^{2/(3-2\mu)} \sim t^{2n-2}$, and peak line mass $M'_{\rm max} \sim t^{1-n}$. For a scale-independent turbulent stress $W^r_\phi \approx w \approx 0.05$ ($\mu = 0, n = 4/3$), General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory (GRTDT) reproduces disk spreading within a factor of $\sim 2$, though it over-predicts the horizon accretion rate by a factor of $\sim 2$ at $t \gtrsim 2\times 10^4\,t_{\rm g}$ because unbound disk winds carry away $\sim 50\%\text{--}80\%$ of the lost mass.
papers.problem: Whether simplified general relativistic thin disk theory (GRTDT) remains applicable to thick ($H/r \sim 1$), magnetically arrested (MAD) accretion flows over secular viscous timescales up to $10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$, and how non-local magnetic torques, disk winds, and turbulent stress affect long-term disk spreading.
papers.method: Ideal GRMHD simulations on a Schwarzschild metric performed with AthenaK using Cartesian Kerr-Schild coordinates, adaptive mesh refinement, and a novel cyclic zoom algorithm to reach $t_{\rm max} = 10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$. These numerical results are compared against analytical Green's function solutions of height-integrated, vertically averaged GRTDT governing equations: $\partial\Sigma/\partial t = (r\overline{U}^t)^{-1}\partial_r [(\overline{U}_\phi')^{-1}\partial_r (r\Sigma W^r_\phi)]$ with turbulent stress parameterization $W^r_\phi = w(r/r_0)^\mu(\rho/\rho_0)^\eta$.
papers.reason: This paper presents the first ultra-long GRMHD simulation of a black hole accretion torus up to $t_{\rm max} = 10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$ and benchmarks it against relativistic thin disk theory, providing valuable insights into the late-time evolution of accretion engines, outflows, and TDE plateau phases.

papers.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
papers.result: The authors derive the perturbation dynamics and coupled dispersion relation for the induced scattering instability, $D_{\rm v}^{2}-f_{0}\Omega_{\rm B}^{2}\simeq\frac{2\eta^{3}}{\omega}k(\Omega+k)\left(\frac{1}{D_{+}}+\frac{1}{D_{-}}\right)$, where $D_{\rm v}\equiv\Omega+v_{x}k$, $D_{\pm}\equiv(\Omega\pm\omega)^{2}-k^{2}-\omega_{\rm p}^{2}$, and the scattering parameter is $\eta\equiv\omega({\cal A}\varepsilon_{\rm p}/2)^{2/3}$. In the strong-coupling limit ($\Omega_{\rm B}\ll\eta$), the maximum growth rate scales as $\Gamma_{\rm gr}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\eta$, while in the weak-coupling limit ($\Omega_{\rm B}\gg\eta$), the instability growth is modified by the magnetic restoring frequency $\Omega_{\rm B}\equiv\sqrt{1+\hat{a}^{2}/2}(\omega_{\rm B}/\gamma_{0})$.

papers.method: A cold two-fluid perturbation model in the wave frame combined with harmonic expansions across the fundamental frequency $\Omega$ and sidebands $\Omega\pm\omega$, complemented by kinetic PIC simulations using OSIRIS with the Higuera & Cary particle pusher.
