papers.title: Discovery of a New Electron Spectrum Produced by Fast Cooling of Relativistic Electrons
papers.result: In the fast-cooling regime below the minimum injection Lorentz factor ($\gamma_e < \gamma_m$), the time-evolving cooled electron spectrum follows the smooth broken power-law form $f_{\rm U}(\gamma_e,t) = A(t) \gamma_e^{-2} [1 + \gamma_0(t)/\gamma_e]^{-\beta}$, scaling asymptotically as $\gamma_e^{-2}$ for $\gamma_e \gg \gamma_0(t)$ and $\gamma_e^{-2+\beta}$ for $\gamma_e \ll \gamma_0(t)$. For pure synchrotron cooling with $B \propto t^{-b}$ and injection rate $R_{\rm inj} \propto t^q$, $A(t) = \frac{h_0}{g_0}t^{2b+q}$, $\gamma_0(t) = \frac{2b-1}{g_0}t^{2b-1}$, and $\beta = \frac{2b+q}{2b-1}$; with adiabatic cooling included (expansion $\dot{\gamma}_{\rm ad} = -\frac{2}{3t}\gamma_e$), $\gamma_0(t) = \frac{6b-1}{3g_0}t^{2b-1}$ and $\beta = \frac{6b+3q+2}{6b-1}$.
papers.problem: In astrophysical relativistic jets such as GRBs and blazars, electrons below the minimum injection Lorentz factor $\gamma_m$ evolve in a non-steady state, causing their energy distribution to deviate significantly from the canonical steady-state power law $f(\gamma_e) \propto \gamma_e^{-2}$.
papers.method: Analytical kinetic integration and differential equation solving of electron cooling trajectories $\dot{\gamma}_e = -g(t)\gamma_e^2 - \frac{2}{3t}\gamma_e$ combined with exact verification against the source-free Fokker-Planck equation $\frac{\partial f}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial}{\partial \gamma_e} [\dot{\gamma}_e f] = 0$ for $\gamma_e < \gamma_m$.
papers.reason: The paper provides an analytical, unified fast-cooling electron spectrum $f_{\rm U}(\gamma_e, t) = A(t) \gamma_e^{-2} [1 + \gamma_0(t)/\gamma_e]^{-\beta}$ for non-steady relativistic jet systems (GRBs, blazars), solving the long-standing discrepancy from the standard steady-state $\gamma_e^{-2}$ distribution below $\gamma_m$.

papers.title: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection
papers.result: Coherent fast magnetosonic waves are stably excited via flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection, yielding a radiation efficiency of $\eta \sim 7 \times 10^{-4}$ for $B_g/B_0 = 0$ and $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2) \times 10^{-3}$ for moderate guide fields ($B_g/B_0 = 0.1\text{--}0.3$). The escaping radiation is 100% linearly polarized X-mode ($\,\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), with a polarization angle offset between opposite sides of the sheet of $\Delta\mathrm{PA} \sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.
papers.problem: Whether 3D relativistic instabilities (e.g., relativistic drift kink instability and flux rope kink instability) and realistic outflow boundaries suppress coherent radio wave emission found in simplified 2D periodic relativistic reconnection simulations.
papers.method: 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of pair plasmas using TRISTAN-MP with open outflow boundaries along $x$ ($L_x=1600\,c/\omega_p$, $L_z=816\,c/\omega_p$), cold magnetization $\sigma = B_0^2/(4\pi n_0 m c^2) = 10$, and guide fields $B_g/B_0 \in \{0, 0.1, 0.3\}$, diagnosing wave Poynting flux $S_{\mathrm{wave}}=(c/4\pi)(\delta E_{z}\delta B_{x}-\delta E_{x}\delta B_{z})$ and efficiency $\eta \equiv S_{\mathrm{wave}}/S_0$.
papers.reason: This work presents 3D PIC simulations of coherent radio emission from flux rope mergers in relativistic reconnection with outflow boundary conditions and guide fields, directly testing FRB and pulsar emission engine models.

papers.title: An intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion in the Small Magellanic Cloud
papers.result: The binary has an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb} = 19.95 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$ ($19.947 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$), radial velocity semi-amplitude $K = 91.7^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and eccentricity $e = 0.032^{+0.031}_{-0.022}$, yielding a binary mass function $f_m \approx 0.066\,M_\odot$. The stripped star has an evolutionary mass $M_{\rm evol} = 3.840 \pm 0.535\,M_\odot$ ($M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84 \pm 0.54\,M_\odot$), $T_{\rm eff} = 68.3 \pm 6.4\,{\rm kK}$, $\log(g/[{\rm cm\,s^{-2}}]) = 4.76 \pm 0.12$, radius $R = 0.99 \pm 0.09\,R_\odot$, luminosity $\log(L/L_\odot) = 4.28 \pm 0.13$, and an anomalously high surface hydrogen mass fraction $X_{\rm H,s} = 0.625^{+0.012}_{-0.011}\,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.035\,(\mathrm{sys})$. For $M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84\,M_\odot$, the companion's minimum mass is $M_2 = 1.19\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$) with a median of $1.41\,M_\odot$. Optical light curve limits rule out main-sequence companions (which would produce reflection variability $\ge 10\%$ vs observed limit $\lesssim 1\%$), and X-ray non-detection sets $L_X \lesssim 9 \times 10^{33}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($0.2-12\,{\rm keV}$), highly consistent with a neutron star companion.
papers.problem: Intermediate-mass stripped stars ($M \approx 2-7\,M_\odot$) in compact orbits with compact objects are key theoretical evolutionary precursors to stripped/ultra-stripped core-collapse supernovae and double compact object mergers, yet observational identifications of such binaries remain exceedingly sparse.
papers.method: Target selection via SMASH $u$-band excess, Gaia astrometric membership, and follow-up multi-epoch intermediate-resolution spectroscopy (MagE and GMOS-S). Radial velocities were obtained by cross-correlation $\chi^2$ minimization against non-LTE stripped-star synthetic spectra and fitted with The Joker and MCMC (`emcee`). Atmospheric and physical parameters were determined via joint SED and non-LTE spectral fitting combined with MESA stellar evolutionary models ($Z = 0.002$). Companion irradiation constraints were simulated with PHOEBE against 3860 epochs of OGLE $I$-band light curves, coupled with XMM-Newton flux limits and Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion rate modeling.
papers.reason: The paper reports the discovery and orbital/stellar characterization of SMASH J004005-733351 in the SMC, an intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion (minimum mass $M_2 \gtrsim 1.2\,M_\odot$, likely a neutron star). This system serves as a direct progenitor benchmark for stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae (Type Ib/ultra-stripped SNe) and double neutron star mergers.

papers.title: CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker--Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations
papers.result: CROMA implements an implicit Chang-Cooper scheme solved via Parallel Cyclic Reduction (PCR) on GPUs, achieving a tridiagonal solve throughput saturating at $R_{\rm solve} \approx 10^{3}\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per MPI task, an end-to-end wall-clock throughput of $R_{\rm wall} \approx 400\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per task at $N_{\rm trc} \sim 10^6$ ($N_{\rm bin} = 128$), an acceleration factor of $\sim 10\times$ compared to 32 CPU cores, and a synchrotron emissivity computation speedup by a factor of $N_\theta \approx 10^3$ using precomputed tables.
papers.problem: Cosmological fluid simulations cannot resolve the microphysical evolution of cosmic-ray energy spectra over millions of Lagrangian tracers due to the prohibitive computational cost of Fokker-Planck solvers on CPUs.
papers.method: One-dimensional momentum Fokker-Planck equation $\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial}{\partial p}\left[D_{pp}\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial p}+\left(H(p,z(t))-\frac{2}{p}D_{pp}\right)\mathcal{N}(p)\right] - \frac{\mathcal{N}}{T(p)} + Q(p,z(t))$ discretized via the Chang-Cooper finite difference scheme; tridiagonal system solved on GPUs using the PCR algorithm with $\mathcal{O}(N_{\rm bin}\log_2 N_{\rm bin})$ complexity; hadronic secondary creation ($pp \to \pi^{\pm, 0}$) and precomputed 2D lookup tables for pitch-angle-integrated synchrotron emission $j_\nu(\nu_l, B)$.
papers.reason: The paper presents CROMA, a GPU-accelerated Fokker-Planck solver for post-processing cosmological MHD simulations along Lagrangian tracer particles, incorporating cosmic ray protons, secondary electrons/neutrinos/gamma-rays via pp collisions, stochastic re-acceleration, and synchrotron emission.

papers.title: Phase-Twist Instability in a Coprecessing Neutrino Plasma
papers.result: The authors identify a gapless phase-twist hydrodynamic instability for coprecessing neutrino polarization vectors with dispersion $\Upsilon_{\mu\nu}K^{\mu}K^{\nu}=0$ (i.e. $\omega^{2}\Upsilon_{00}+k^{2}\Upsilon_{11}+\omega k(\Upsilon_{01}+\Upsilon_{10})=0$), yielding imaginary frequencies $\mathrm{Im}(\omega)=\gamma \sim k\Delta v\Delta\theta$ in the hydrodynamic regime and saturating at maximum growth rate $\gamma_{\rm max}\sim |\vec{H}_{\bf p}|\Delta\theta^{2}$ around $k\sim |\vec{H}_{\bf p}|\Delta\theta/\Delta v$.
papers.problem: Whether dense neutrino plasmas exhibiting flavor-nondiagonal coprecession backgrounds (such as those generating spectral splits in core-collapse supernovae) are dynamically stable against space-dependent perturbations.
papers.method: Mean-field neutrino flavor kinetic equations in a rotating frame, hydrodynamic effective action formulation $\mathcal{S}_{\rm eff}=\frac{1}{2}\int dtdz\sum_{{\bf p},{\bf p}^{\prime}}(\partial_{t}\delta\Phi+v\partial_{z}\delta\Phi)\mathcal{K}^{-1}_{{\bf p},{\bf p}^{\prime}}(\partial_{t}\delta\Phi+v^{\prime}\partial_{z}\delta\Phi)$, and linear stability analysis decomposed into flavor-helicity states $\psi_{\pm,{\bf p}}=x_{\bf p}\pm iy_{\bf p}$.
papers.reason: The paper presents the first explicit dispersion relation and instability analysis about a flavor-nondiagonal background in dense neutrino plasmas, relevant to core-collapse/electron-capture supernova prompt bursts.

papers.title: Dynamical constraints on the companion mass from pulsar timing and cyclotron line confirmation in the SFXT IGR J16418-4532
papers.result: Coherent pulsations are measured at $P_{\mathrm{spin}} = 1208.67 \pm 0.04\mathrm{\ s}$ (NuSTAR) and $P_{\mathrm{spin}} = 1209.4178 \pm 0.0084\mathrm{\ s}$ (RXTE/PCA), with projected semi-major axes $a_{x}\sin i = 55.1 \pm 3.5\mathrm{\ lt\text{-}s}$ and $51.3 \pm 2.6\mathrm{\ lt\text{-}s}$, respectively. Combined with binary geometry and Roche-lobe constraints, the companion star mass is constrained to $M_{\mathrm{c}} \simeq 12\text{--}18\ M_{\odot}$ and radius $R_{\mathrm{c}} \simeq 13\text{--}16\ R_{\odot}$. The confirmed CRSF at $E_{\mathrm{cyc}} \sim 50\mathrm{\ keV}$ implies a neutron star surface magnetic field of $B \approx 5 \times 10^{12}\mathrm{\ G}$.
papers.problem: Severe X-ray luminosity variations and pulse profile instability in SFXTs prevent classical pulse time-of-arrival (TOA) fitting, leaving binary orbital parameters, companion masses, and magnetic field strengths poorly constrained.
papers.method: Applied epoch-folding search over a grid of orbital delays parameterized by projected semi-major axis $a_{x}\sin i$ assuming a circular orbit ($e=0$, $P_{\mathrm{orb}} = 3.73881\mathrm{\ d}$) to maximize pulse detection significance, followed by NuSTAR spectral fitting (NPEX, CompTT) with Monte Carlo significance testing for the cyclotron resonance scattering feature.
papers.reason: This study derives the first dynamical constraints on the companion mass of a supergiant fast X-ray transient (SFXT) and confirms a $\sim 50\mathrm{\ keV}$ cyclotron line, providing critical observational constraints on accreting neutron star parameters.

papers.title: NOCTURNE. VI. Hour-timescale radio variability in early-stage active galactic nucleus SDSS J122844.81+501751.2
papers.result: The target SDSS J122844.81+501751.2 displays extreme hour-timescale variability at $37\ \mathrm{GHz}$ with an $e$-folding timescale as short as $\tau = 1.1\ \mathrm{h}$ between MRO $37\ \mathrm{GHz}$ and JVLA $33\ \mathrm{GHz}$ measurements. The implied variability brightness temperature reaches $T_{\rm b,var} \sim 10^{17}-10^{18}\ \mathrm{K}$, well in excess of the inverse Compton limit, requiring Doppler factors $\delta_{\rm var} \approx 140-400$. Swift XRT spectroscopy gives a soft photon index $\Gamma = 2.33^{+0.20}_{-0.18}$ and unabsorbed $0.3-10\ \mathrm{keV}$ flux of $7.5^{+0.9}_{-0.7} \times 10^{-13}\ \mathrm{erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$.
papers.problem: Unraveling the physical origin and radiation mechanism of extreme, hour-timescale radio flaring in early-stage active galactic nuclei harboring low-mass supermassive black holes near the Eddington limit.
papers.method: Multi-epoch, coordinated observations with MRO ($37\ \mathrm{GHz}$), OVRO ($15\ \mathrm{GHz}$), JVLA ($10, 22, 33\ \mathrm{GHz}$), and the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory (XRT and UVOT). Flare exponential parameters are modeled as $\Delta S(t) = \Delta S_{\mathrm{max}}\mathrm{e}^{|t-t_{\mathrm{max}}|/\tau}$ to compute $T_{\rm b,var} = 1.548\times 10^{-32} \frac{\Delta S_{\mathrm{max}}d_{L}^{2}}{\nu^{2}\tau^{2}(1+z)}\ [\mathrm{K}]$ and Doppler factor $\delta_{\rm var} = (T_{\rm b,var}/T_{\rm b,int})^{1/3}$.
papers.reason: The paper reports the fastest intrinsic radio variability observed in an active galactic nucleus to date, constraining relativistic Doppler boosting and magnetic eruption physics in early-stage AGNs.

papers.title: Reconstruction of very inclined air showers with radio data and application to the first GRANDProto300 cosmic-ray candidates
papers.result: On realistic GP300 simulations, the ADF reconstruction achieves an angular resolution better than $0.07^\circ$ and a primary energy resolution $<15\%$. Applied to raw ADC data from 65 deployed antennas of GRANDProto300, it successfully identified 51 high-quality cosmic-ray candidate events with an illustrative event showing reconstructed direction $\theta = 75.1^\circ \pm 0.03^\circ$, $\phi = 358.7^\circ \pm 0.02^\circ$, reduced $\chi^2_{\nu,\mathrm{ADF}} = 4.7$, and primary energy $E = 2.08 \times 10^{18}\text{ eV}$.
papers.problem: Reconstructing the full geometry (shower axis and emission source) and primary energy of very inclined air showers with sub-degree accuracy in autonomous radio arrays without requiring full electric-field deconvolution.
papers.method: The method first fits a spherical wavefront to trigger times to obtain the point-like emission origin $X_{\mathrm{source}}$, accounting for atmospheric refraction. The shower axis $(\theta, \phi)$ and scaling amplitude $A$ are then fitted by minimizing $R(\theta,\phi) = \sum_{i=1}^{N_{\rm ant}} [A_{i} - f_{i}^{\rm ADF}(A,\theta,\phi,\delta\omega;X_{e})]^2$, with the ADF profile parameterized as $f^{\rm ADF} = \frac{A}{l}\left[1+G_{A}\frac{\cos\eta}{\sin\alpha}\right] \left[1+4\left(\frac{\tan\omega/\tan\omega_{c}-1}{\delta\omega}\right)^{2}\right]^{-1}$, yielding electromagnetic energy proxy $E^{*}_{\rm em} = \frac{A}{\sin(\alpha)\,f(\rho,\sin(\alpha))}$.
papers.reason: The paper demonstrates the Angular Distribution Function (ADF) method for reconstructing very inclined air showers using raw radio antenna voltages, which directly supports the detection pipeline for ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and Earth-skimming tau neutrinos in GRAND.

papers.title: Three-flavor neutrino Boltzmann transport and flavor instabilities in long-lived neutron-star merger remnants
papers.problem: Previous simulations of neutron-star merger remnants commonly adopted effective two-flavor approximations (assuming indistinguishable $\nu_\mu$ and $\nu_\tau$) and phenomenological subgrid models, which fail to capture the impact of muonization physics and three-flavor non-linear quantum kinetic coherence on flavor instability criteria.
papers.method:
Hydrodynamical profiles from a 3D general relativistic M1 merger simulation ($2.5\,M_\odot$ remnant at $ ar{t} \simeq 30\,\mathrm{ms}$) are mapped into the axisymmetric GR Boltzmann solver Gmunu coupled with the Weakhub reaction library. The framework solves the six-dimensional Boltzmann equation for all six neutrino species ($npe\mu$ matter) incorporating complete muonic charged- and neutral-current reactions, regularized in the dilute-muon limit via a Broyden-based nested implicit solver. Linear stability analyses (LSA) and subsequent local 3-flavor momentum-dependent QKE simulations $(\partial_{t} + \mathbf{v}\cdot
abla)\varrho = -i[H_{
u
u},\varrho] + \mathcal{C}$ are performed to determine growth rates and non-linear asymptotic saturation states.
papers.reason: This work performs full six-dimensional, three-flavor Boltzmann neutrino transport in a long-lived binary neutron star merger remnant, systematically revealing how muonic weak interactions and three-flavor coupling reshape fast and collisional flavor instabilities.

papers.title: 2:1 Harmonics in the Radio Light Curves of Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidates
papers.result: Systematic sine-wave fits to radio monitoring light curves demonstrate robust 2:1 period commensurabilities in SMBHB candidates PKS J0805$-$0111, PKS J1309+1154, and PKS 2131$-$021, where subtracting fundamental and harmonic modes reduces residual variance by 50%–65% and 20%–44%, respectively. In the gravitational-wave-dominated inspiral regime with orbit shrinkage timescale $t_{\rm GR}\propto r^{4}$, the detection incidence scales with baseline duration $\tau$ as $N_2/N_1 = [\tau_2/\tau_1]^{8/3}$, explaining the scarcity of short-period ($P < 1\text{ yr}$) systems. For secondary companion-induced modulation, orbital radius and velocity scale as $r/10^{16}\,{\rm cm} \sim 1.5 P_y^{2/3} M_{P9}^{1/3}$ and $v/10^9\,{\rm cm\,s^{-1}} \sim 3 P_y^{-1/3} M_{P9}^{1/3}$, balancing the disk wind magnetic pressure $B_W \sim L_{j\,44}^{1/2} r_{16}^{-1}\,{\rm G}$ at $r_*/r \sim 0.2 L_{j44}^{1/2} M_{P9}^{1/3} P_y^{-1/3}$.
papers.problem: Distinguishing genuine orbital/Doppler-induced 2:1 harmonic modulations from false-positive periodic signals generated by steep power spectral density (PSD) red-noise stochastic flares in blazar radio light curves.
papers.method: Multi-component Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sine-wave fits accounting for correlated red noise via covariance matrices and intrinsic jitter $\sigma_0$ with log-likelihood $\ln\mathcal{L}=-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left[\frac{(S_{i}-S(t_{i}))^{2}}{\sigma_{i}^{2}+\sigma_{0}^{2}}+\ln(\sigma_{i}^{2}+\sigma_{0}^{2})\right]$ applied to multi-decadal OVRO and UMRAO monitoring databases, alongside relativistic jet Doppler kinematic and disk-wind interaction models.
papers.reason: The paper investigates 2:1 harmonic and subharmonic periodicities in radio light curves of supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB) candidates, testing relativistic jet Doppler boosting, disk-wind interactions, and gravitational-wave-driven population statistics.

papers.title: A microscopic analysis of shear acceleration in the relativistic regime
papers.result: Particle shear acceleration in inhomogeneous relativistic velocity fields is governed by the effective shear tensor $\sigma(x) = \tilde{\sigma}/\gamma_{\rm J}$, which decreases in highly relativistic regions. When $\sigma \tau' \gtrsim 1$, the return time distribution between crossing events exhibits a heavy-tailed power-law $p(t_{\rm cross}) \propto t_{\rm cross}^{-1.27}$, driving sub-diffusive momentum gain ($\langle p^{\prime 2}\rangle \propto t^q, q < 1$) and causing a spectral transition/hardening at $\sigma \tau'(p') \sim 1$ from gradual shear ($n(p') \propto p'^{-2}$ for $\delta=1$) to an intermittent non-gradual acceleration branch.
papers.problem: Standard Fokker-Planck transport models of shear acceleration assume gradual acceleration ($\tau' \sigma \ll 1$) with small momentum increments per scattering and often approximate the shear rate as spatially constant, which fails when particle mean free paths become comparable to the shear gradient scale or across relativistic velocity jumps.
papers.method: A covariant stochastic differential equation (SDE) formulation based on the generalized Fermi acceleration framework tracking comoving momentum $p'$ and directional cosines $\mu_i'$, where pitch-angle scattering is implemented via an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with scattering frequency $\nu' = 1/\tau'$ and validated against continuous-time random walk (CTRW) models.
papers.reason: The paper presents a covariant microscopic framework beyond standard Fokker-Planck gradual shear acceleration in relativistic jets, revealing sub-diffusive momentum transport and spectral hardening relevant to cosmic-ray and high-energy particle acceleration in relativistic transient outflows.

papers.title: Quasiparticle Modeling of Strange Quark Stars with In-Medium QCD Effects at Finite Temperature and Strong Magnetic Fields
papers.result: At $B = 10^{15}\,\mathrm{G}$, increasing temperature from $T = 0$ to $50\,\mathrm{MeV}$ stiffens the EoS, boosting the maximum gravitational mass from $M_{\max} = 1.66\,M_{\odot}$ ($R = 9.48\,\mathrm{km}$) to $2.19\,M_{\odot}$ (compatible with PSR J0740+6620 and PSR J0952-0607). Conversely, ultra-strong fields ($B = 10^{19}\,\mathrm{G}$ at $T = 50\,\mathrm{MeV}$) induce Maxwell stress $\propto B^2/(8\pi)$ that softens the configuration, reducing $M_{\max}$ to $0.99\,M_{\odot}$ ($R = 5.41\,\mathrm{km}$). The sound speed satisfies causality and asymptotically approaches the conformal limit $v_s^2 \rightarrow 1/3$ at high densities, with low-mass radii scaling as $R \propto M^{1/3}$.
papers.problem: Constructing a thermodynamically consistent equation of state for strange quark matter under finite temperatures and extreme magnetic fields to support massive compact stars ($M \gtrsim 2.0\,M_{\odot}$) while satisfying local charge neutrality and $\beta$-equilibrium.
papers.method: A thermodynamic quasiparticle model (QPM) incorporating an in-medium effective quark mass $m_i^*(T,\mu_i) = \frac{m_i}{2} + \sqrt{\frac{m_i^2}{4} + \frac{g_i^2 Q_i^2}{6\pi^2}}$ with renormalization scale $Q_i = \sqrt{\mu_i^2 + (\pi T)^2}$ and magnetic running coupling $\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{mag}}(B) = 1 + \alpha\ln(1 + \beta eB/\Lambda_2^2)$, coupled to a state-dependent bag constant $B^*(\mu,T)$ and total energy density $\epsilon_{\rm tot} = \epsilon_{\rm kin} + \epsilon_{\rm mag} + B^* + B^2/(8\pi)$, solved via the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff (TOV) equations.
papers.reason: The paper investigates the equation of state (EoS) and maximum mass of magnetized, finite-temperature strange quark stars using a thermodynamically consistent quasiparticle model, providing microphysical constraints relevant to high-energy compact objects and massive pulsars.

papers.title: History of Turn-Ons - the irregular 35-day clock - of Hercules X-1
papers.result: Turn-Ons preferentially occur at binary orbital phases $\Phi_{\rm orb} \sim 0.25$ and $\sim 0.75$, with quantized cycle durations concentrated at $20.0$, $20.5$ (accounting for $\sim 57\%$), and $21.0 \times P_{\rm orb}$ ($P_{\rm orb} = 1.70016759\,\mathrm{d}$). The long-term $(O-C)$ timing residual curve reveals two distinct parabolic segments separated by Anomalous Low 3 (AL3): pre-AL3 has $P = 34.95\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-1.8 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$, while post-AL3 has $P = 35.03\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-5.30 \pm 0.23) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$. Anomalous Lows recur with a mean period of $(5.35 \pm 0.03)\,\mathrm{yr}$.
papers.problem: Unraveling the timing regularity, quantized phase transitions, and physical drivers behind the irregular $\sim 35\,\mathrm{d}$ super-orbital clock and quasi-periodic Anomalous Lows in Her X-1 over multi-decade baselines.
papers.method:
Compiled and analyzed 55 years of X-ray monitoring data across 570 cycles (UHURU to Swift/BAT, MAXI, and Fermi/GBM). Turn-On is formally defined as the time when X-ray flux reaches $30\%$ of the subsequent Main-On peak flux. Light curves are modeled via a double-Fermi empirical formulation:
$${\rm F}(t) = A_{0} \times \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(\frac{A_{1}-t}{A_{2}}\right)} \times \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(\frac{t-A_{3}}{A_{4}}\right)}$$\nResiduals are computed using $(O - C) = 0$ at cycle #31 (MJD 42409.9) with reference duration $20.5 \times P_{\rm orb} = 34.8534356\,\mathrm{d}$.
papers.reason: This work presents a comprehensive 55-year timing analysis of the 35-day super-orbital cycle of the accreting neutron star Hercules X-1, establishing fundamental observational constraints on tilted/warped accretion disk precession and compact object high-energy phenomenology.

papers.title: FLITS: an interactive, reproducible workbench for fast radio burst analysis
papers.result: FLITS unifies FRB data inspection, RFI mitigation, burst property extraction (signal-to-noise ratio, peak flux density, fluence, widths, and arrival times), burst-model fitting, and weighted RM synthesis ($Q, U, V$ polarization analysis) into reproducible JSON session states with checksum validation.
papers.problem: FRB post-detection properties (DM, RM, scattering, sub-burst structure) depend heavily on subjective user choices (interference masking, background/burst region selection, time-frequency resolution), and automated DM optimization often fails or creates degeneracies with downward frequency drifting (the 'sad-trombone' effect) without interactive checks and reproducible session tracking.
papers.method: The tool provides an interactive browser GUI and command-line interface (`flits measure`, `flits replay`). It supports multi-format data ingestion (SIGPROC filterbank, PSRFITS, CHIME/FRB HDF5), implements DM scoring metrics (S/N, `DM_phase` burst-structure, and smoothed-structure metric reporting DM uncertainty ranges), weighted RM synthesis ($P(\lambda^2) \propto \int F(\phi) e^{2i\phi\lambda^2} d\phi$), and integrated dynamic spectrum burst modeling based on `fitburst`.
papers.reason: FLITS is an open-source interactive workbench and pipeline tool for FRB dynamic spectrum analysis, DM optimization, polarization/RM synthesis, and model fitting (fitburst integration). While it is an astronomical software package rather than an observational discovery or theoretical breakthrough, it is directly useful for analyzing multi-telescope FRB data and checking dispersion and polarization properties.

papers.title: Self lensing in BH-NS binaries as progenitors for periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts
papers.result: Pure Keplerian self-lensing fails with a tiny activity window $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{KP}} \sim \mathcal{O}(0.5\,\mathrm{hours})$, whereas Lense-Thirring precession with period $\tau_{\mathrm{LT}} = \frac{\pi(1-e^{2})^{3/2}c^{3}a^{3}}{G^{2}M_{\mathrm{BH}}^{2}\chi} = 2\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ reproduces wide activity windows $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{LT}} \sim 0.5\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ for small inclinations $i \sim (5\text{--}8) \times 10^{-2}\,{^\circ}$. Splitting time delays $\tau_{\mathrm{lens}}^{\mathrm{Spl}} \approx \frac{4GM_{\mathrm{BH}}}{c^3}(1+z)\lambda(r_s/a)^{1/2} \sim 10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}$ match the observed millisecond waiting-time peak in FRB 20121102A, constraining the companion mass to $M_{\mathrm{BH}} \sim 10^3\text{--}10^4\,M_\odot$ with maximum amplification $\mathcal{A}_{\max} \approx \sqrt{8r_{s}a/R^{2}} \sim 10^4$ and gravitational wave merger timescale $\tau_{\mathrm{GW}} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{yr}$.
papers.problem: Periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts (prFRBs) exhibit broad periodic activity windows ($30\%\text{--}50\%$ of their period) and pulse energies orders of magnitude higher than Galactic magnetars, which existing free-precession, stellar-wind eclipse, or simple orbital models struggle to simultaneously explain.
papers.method: The authors construct a post-Newtonian binary dynamics and gravitational self-lensing framework using the Maeder-Liebes finite-source weak-field approximation $L_{\rm Lensed} = g^4 \mathcal{A} L_{\rm NS}$, incorporating Lense-Thirring and pericenter precession $\langle d\Omega/dt \rangle = \frac{2G^2 M_{\rm BH}^2}{c^3 a^3 (1-e^2)^{3/2}} \chi$, relativistic timing delays (Rømer, Einstein, and Shapiro), and Monte Carlo simulations of magnetar-like log-normal pulse distributions.
papers.reason: The paper presents a quantitative gravitational self-lensing scenario in BH-NS binaries driven by Lense-Thirring precession to explain periodically repeating FRBs and pulse energy magnification. It derives critical constraints on intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) companions and pulse delay timescales directly relevant to FRB burst morphology and environmental modeling.

papers.title: X-ray Emission Study of TeV Blazars
papers.result: Luminosity correlations show $\log L_{\rm TeV}$ correlates positively with soft X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.54 \pm 0.20$, $r = 0.63$) and hard X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.23 \pm 0.28$, $r = 0.52$), consistent with leptonic scenarios. X-ray luminosity correlates strongly with disk luminosity $\log L_{\rm disk}$ ($r = 0.61$ soft, $r = 0.77$ hard) but lacks significant correlation with black hole mass $\log M_{\rm BH}$ ($p=0.21$ and $0.77$). The majority of well-sampled sources exhibit log-normal soft X-ray flux distributions with PSD slopes $\beta_{\rm PSD} \sim 1.0\text{--}1.6$.
papers.problem: Unraveling the relativistic jet particle acceleration and emission mechanisms (leptonic vs hadronic processes) and understanding how central engine properties ($M_{\rm BH}$, $L_{\rm disk}$) regulate high-energy emission in TeV blazars.
papers.method: Extracted 9833 Swift-XRT and 140 NuSTAR spectra, performing spectral fits with power-law and log-parabola models. Timing and stochastic behavior were evaluated using the fractional variability amplitude $F_{\rm var} = \sqrt{[\frac{1}{N-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(x_{i}-\overline{x})^{2}-\overline{\sigma_{\rm err}^{2}}]/\mu^{2}}$, PDF flux distribution fitting, and PSD slope $\beta_{\rm PSD}$ constraints from MFVF forward modeling under $P(f) \propto f^{-\beta_{\rm PSD}}$.
papers.reason: The paper presents a comprehensive X-ray spectral and timing analysis of 85 TeV blazars using Swift-XRT and NuSTAR data, investigating relativistic jet emission mechanisms and disk-jet coupling.

papers.title: Searches for new particle physics by methods of classical and neutrino astronomy
papers.result: The review synthesizes constraints on new physics across stellar laboratories, transient photon propagation, and neutrino telescopes. For axion-electron coupling from globular cluster TRGB calibrations, the 95% CL bound reaches $g_{ae} < 6.4 \times 10^{-14}$ via electron bremsstrahlung energy loss $\varepsilon_a \propto g_{ae}^2 T^4$. For high-energy photon propagation from GRB 221009A ($z \simeq 0.151$), photon-ALP mixing ($m_a \simeq 5.2 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{eV}$, $g_{a\gamma} \simeq 6 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$) and subluminal quadratic LIV ($E_{{\rm LIV},2} \sim 4 \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{GeV}$) are tested against LHAASO ($>10\,\mathrm{TeV}$) and Carpet-3 ($E_\gamma = 300^{+43}_{-38}\,\mathrm{TeV}$) observations, with an allowed host magnetic field window $1.3\,g_{11}^{-1} \lesssim B/\mu\mathrm{G} \lesssim 4.2\,g_{11}$. For neutrino astronomy, superheavy dark matter ($m_X \gg 10^2\,\mathrm{TeV}$) is bounded to lifetimes $\tau_X \gtrsim 10^{26}\text{--}10^{28}\,\mathrm{s}$, and neutrino flavor ratios evolve from source states (e.g., standard $(1:2:0)_S$ or muon-damped $(0:1:0)_S$) toward $(1:1:1)_\oplus$ across cosmic baselines.
papers.problem: How to robustly test beyond-the-Standard-Model physics (axion-like particles, Lorentz-invariance violation, magnetic monopoles, and superheavy dark matter) using astrophysical systems—including stellar evolution clocks, photon propagation anomalies in ultra-luminous transients like GRB 221009A, and large-volume neutrino telescope flavor/diffuse flux observations—while disentangling source physics and observational systematics.

papers.reason: This review provides an extensive astroparticle synthesis directly intersecting core high-energy transient interests, focusing on Lorentz-invariance violation (LIV) and photon-ALP mixing constrained by extreme transient GRB 221009A, as well as astrophysical neutrino flavor ratios and diffuse fluxes.

papers.title: An SRG/eROSITA Study of Be X-ray binaries in Quiescence
papers.result: Detections in the $0.5-10\ \mathrm{keV}$ range reveal quiescent X-ray luminosities spanning $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 10^{33}-10^{36}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, with photon indices $\Gamma \sim 0.5-2.0$ and blackbody temperatures $kT_{\rm bb} \sim 0.8-1.6\ \mathrm{keV}$ from emitting radii $R \sim 0.1-2\ \mathrm{km}$. A power-law correlation connects X-ray luminosity and emission radius as $L \propto R^{\alpha}$ with index $\alpha = 2.3 \pm 0.2$. In addition, upper limits on non-detected sources (e.g. 2S 1553$-$542 and RX J0812.4$-$3114) fall below the theoretical propeller luminosity $L_{\rm prop} \simeq 4\times 10^{37}k^{7/2}B_{12}^{2}P^{-7/3}M_{1.4}^{-2/3}R_{6}^{5}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, confirming propeller or cold disc inhibition.
papers.problem: Determining the accretion mechanisms and emission states (such as the propeller phase, cold disc accretion, or deep crustal heating) governing neutron star Be X-ray binaries at very low mass-transfer rates during quiescence.
papers.method: Analysis of SRG/eROSITA eRASS1 survey data ($0.2-8\ \mathrm{keV}$) using Cash statistics and Akaike Information Criterion ($\mathrm{AIC} = 2k + C$) in XSPEC to fit absorbed power-law (`tbabs*powerlaw`) and absorbed blackbody (`tbabs*bbodyrad`) models, compared against theoretical thresholds for propeller transitions ($L_{\rm prop}$) and cold disk accretion ($L_{\rm cold}$).
papers.reason: This paper presents a systematic eROSITA eRASS1 survey of Galactic Be X-ray binaries in quiescence, providing valuable observational constraints on low-accretion-rate neutron star regimes relevant to compact object high-energy studies.

papers.title: $γ$-ray variability of changing-look blazars: FSRQ-like jet behaviour
papers.result: Changing-look blazars (CLBs) exhibit fractional variability $F_{\rm var} = 0.483$ at a 30-day cadence that is statistically indistinguishable from FSRQs ($0.437$, $p=0.94$) but significantly higher than BL Lacs ($0.262$, $p=1.4\times 10^{-4}$). CLBs have Eddington-scaled accretion disk luminosities $\log(L_{\rm disk}/L_{\rm Edd}) = -1.42$, which are close to FSRQs ($-0.85$) and far above BL Lacs ($-3.36$), confirming that the optical changing-look behavior is driven by jet synchrotron continuum swamping rather than accretion mode transitions.
papers.problem: Whether optical state transitions in changing-look blazars (between FSRQ and BL Lac optical classes) reflect genuine accretion regime transitions (e.g., crossing $L_{\rm disk}/L_{\rm Edd} \sim 10^{-2}$) or are purely caused by relativistic jet continuum variations swamping the broad emission lines.
papers.method: Analysis of 17.9-year Fermi-LAT light curves at 3-day, 7-day, and 30-day cadences for 111 CLBs alongside 4FGL-DR4 FSRQ and BL Lac control samples, measuring fractional variability $F_{\rm var} = \sqrt{S^2 - \overline{\sigma_{\rm err}^2}}/\overline{F}$, power spectral density slopes $P(f) \propto f^{-\beta}$, non-binned log-normal mixture likelihoods, and state occupancy run lengths.
papers.reason: The paper provides a comprehensive 17.9-year Fermi-LAT timing and spectral analysis of changing-look blazars, demonstrating that their relativistic jet variability and central engine Eddington ratios consistently mimic FSRQs rather than BL Lacs.

papers.title: Nonradial oscillation modes of axion condensed neutron stars in the Cowling approximation
papers.result:
The equilibrium background modification shifts $f$- and $p$-mode frequencies upward as $
u_a \equiv m_a / (2\pi)$ increases (for instance, reaching $
u_f = 2.87\,\mathrm{kHz}$, $
u_{p_1} = 8.19\,\mathrm{kHz}$, and $
u_{p_2} = 12.11\,\mathrm{kHz}$ at $
u_a = 15\,\mathrm{kHz}$), while dynamical fluid-axion coupling partially counteracts this shift. When the mode frequency exceeds the threshold $
u_a$, outgoing axion emission damps the fluid modes with damping rate $|\mathrm{Im}\,\omega| \simeq L_a / (2 E_{\mathrm{mode}})$, reaching damping timescales $	au_a = 1/(2\pi |\mathrm{Im}\,
u|) \sim 10\,\mathrm{ms}$. In addition, gravitational atom bound states exhibit hydrogenic eigenvalues $	ilde{k}_n^2 \equiv k_n^2 / m_a^2 = -\alpha^2 / n^2$ with $\omega_n \simeq m_a [1 - \alpha^2/(2n^2)]$ and undergo avoided crossings with fluid $p$-modes accompanied by an inversion of the axion energy fraction $x_a = E_a / (E_a + E_{\mathrm{fluid}})$.
papers.problem: Investigating how finite-density QCD axion condensation in neutron stars affects stellar nonradial oscillations, specifically the frequency shifts, dynamical fluid-axion coupling, and energy loss via axion radiation damping.
papers.method: Solving the linearized nonradial perturbation equations in the relativistic Cowling approximation coupled to the perturbed Klein-Gordon equation $\nabla_\mu \nabla^\mu \delta\theta - m_a^2 \delta\theta = 0$ for a BSk26 static spherical background, using a collocation method matching surface perturbations to exterior outgoing-wave/bound solutions obtained via phase-amplitude and Whittaker asymptotic integrations.
papers.reason: The paper calculates the nonradial ($l=2$) polar oscillation modes of axion-condensed neutron stars under the relativistic Cowling approximation, demonstrating that axion radiation can damp $p$-modes on timescales as short as $\sim 10\,\mathrm{ms}$, which provides a direct theoretical link to neutron star oscillations and compact object high-energy signatures.

papers.title: Impact of Neutrino Trapping on the Equation of State and Structure of Hybrid Stars with 2SC Quark Matter
papers.result: Neutrino trapping ($Y_{Le}=0.4$) robustly shifts the hadron-quark deconfinement transition toward higher baryon densities compared to neutrino-transparent matter. Trapping raises the proton fraction and diminishes the isospin asymmetry $\delta = 1-2Y_p$, which sharply reduces the equation of state's sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry energy slope ($L_{\rm sym} \in [30, 70]~\mathrm{MeV}$) because symmetry-energy energy density scales as $\propto E_{\rm sym}(\varrho)\,\delta^2$. For the reference DDLS50-NJL model ($\eta_D = \eta_V = 1$), maximum gravitational masses are $M_{\max}^{(S=1)} = 2.36\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\max}^{(S=2)} = 2.37\,M_\odot$; varying the vector coupling $\eta_V = G_V/G_S \in [0.8, 1.2]$ alters $M_{\max}$ by $\pm 1.3\%$, while strong diquark pairing ($\eta_D = 1.25$) reduces $M_{\max}$ by up to $-8.5\%$. While Gibbs (global lepton conservation) and Maxwell (local lepton conservation) phase constructions produce nearly indistinguishable macroscopical $M-R$ curves, Gibbs produces a vastly more extended geometric radial mixed-phase core.
papers.problem: How neutrino trapping, diquark pairing (2SC phase), vector repulsion, and phase equilibrium construction (Gibbs vs. Maxwell) affect the equation of state, deconfinement density, and structural profiles of proto-neutron stars and post-merger remnants across nuclear symmetry energy uncertainties.
papers.method: Hadronic matter is modeled via covariant density functional theory (DDLS family with $L_{\rm sym} = 30, 50, 70~\mathrm{MeV}$), while deconfined quark matter is modeled using a three-flavor NJL model with 2SC color superconductivity, repulsive vector interaction $\eta_V = G_V/G_S$, diquark pairing $\eta_D = G_D/G_S$, and a phenomenological bag pressure shift $B^*$. Phase equilibrium is evaluated under global lepton-number conservation (Gibbs construction: $T^H=T^Q$, $\mu_B^H=\mu_B^Q$, $\mu_{Le}^H=\mu_{Le}^Q$, $P_H=P_Q$) versus local conservation (Maxwell benchmark), solving the TOV equations along isentropic profiles ($S = s/(\varrho_B k_B) = 1, 2$) matched to HS(DD2) at crust densities.
papers.reason: The paper investigates the equation of state and structure of hot, lepton-rich proto-neutron stars and merger remnants with two-flavor color-superconducting quark matter, demonstrating that neutrino trapping delays quark deconfinement to higher baryon densities and strongly suppresses the sensitivity to the nuclear symmetry energy slope.

papers.title: Probing the inner disk edge of rotating neutron stars with dipole excitations in finite nuclei
papers.result: Nuclear electric dipole polarizability constraints (CNSP-4 set) reduce the spread in the surface–ISCO transition gravitational mass $M_{\rm tr}(f)$ and equatorial radius $R_{\rm eq}$ across spin frequencies $f$ by factors of $7$--$10$ ($85$--$90\%$ reduction), bringing mass uncertainty below $0.025\,M_{\odot}$ and radius uncertainty below $0.15\text{ km}$. Along the transition, the disk inner-edge Keplerian orbital frequency $\nu_{\rm in} = \Omega_{\rm orb}(R_{\rm in})/(2\pi)$ is confined to a band narrower than $20\text{ Hz}$ (down from $38$--$134\text{ Hz}$ across the full DD–PC family). For the $414\text{ Hz}$ pulsar 4U 0614+09 with highest kHz QPO at $\nu_{\rm QPO} \geq 1267\text{ Hz}$, the allowed mass range is narrowed from $0.81$--$1.97\,M_{\odot}$ to $0.91\lesssim M/M_{\odot}\lesssim 1.97$, and the lower-mass boundary equatorial radius is constrained to $12.40$--$12.71\text{ km}$.
papers.problem: Uncertainties in the nuclear equation of state—especially the density dependence of the nuclear symmetry energy—heavily blur theoretical predictions of whether a neutron star's accretion disk inner edge is truncated by the physical stellar surface ($R_{\rm in} = R_{\rm eq}$) or an external ISCO ($R_{\rm in} = R_{\rm ISCO} > R_{\rm eq}$), hampering the use of kHz QPOs to infer neutron star masses and radii.
papers.method: The authors compute general-relativistic equilibrium sequences of uniformly rotating neutron stars using the RNS code with the DD–PC-J29–J36 family of relativistic energy density functionals ($J = 29$--$36\text{ MeV}$, $L = 29$--$94.1\text{ MeV}$). They isolate the subset compatible with electric dipole polarizabilities of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$, $^{68}\mathrm{Ni}$, $^{120}\mathrm{Sn}$, and $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ (CNSP-4, giving $J = 31.34 \pm 0.79\text{ MeV}$), evaluating the transition condition $R_{\rm ISCO} = R_{\rm eq}$, the orbital frequency $\nu_{\rm in}$, and orbital binding efficiency $\eta_{\rm in} = 1 - E_{\rm in}$.
papers.reason: This study connects nuclear physics dipole polarizability measurements to high-energy observations of compact objects, showing how symmetry-energy constraints restrict the inner accretion disk edge, ISCO transition, and kHz QPO interpretations in neutron star LMXBs.

papers.title: Evidence for a nova super-remnant surrounding the recurrent nova V745 Scorpii using eROSITA
papers.result: eROSITA reveals an elliptical shell with angular size $\sim 19' \times 10'$ (physical dimensions $\sim 90 \times 50\ \mathrm{pc}$ at $d \sim 7.8\text{--}8.2\ \mathrm{kpc}$) with peak emission in the $0.5\text{--}1.2\ \mathrm{keV}$ range. Annular photometry in the $16'\text{--}24'$ shell region yields an unabsorbed X-ray flux of $\sim 2\times 10^{-12}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}\ cm^{-2}}$ and net luminosity $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 1.6\times 10^{34}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, nested inside a larger infrared dust cavity peaking at $\sim 46'$ ($\sim 100\ \mathrm{pc}$).
papers.problem: Recurrent nova outbursts are predicted to sweep up interstellar gas into giant $\sim 100\ \mathrm{pc}$ cavities, where subsequent high-velocity ejecta should shock-heat the inner cavity boundary to emit extended X-rays, but direct observational confirmation of such an X-ray NSR shell remained unconfirmed.
papers.method: The authors analyze $0.2\text{--}2.3\ \mathrm{keV}$ eROSITA survey observations with annular background-subtracted photometry modeled via absorbed thermal plasma (`TBabs * vapec`, $N_{\mathrm{H}}=2.8\times 10^{21}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$). They conduct 1D hydrodynamic simulations with the Morpheus code modeling recurrent outbursts ($P = 26\ \mathrm{yr}$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}} = 10^{-7}\ M_{\odot}$, $v_{\mathrm{ej}} = 4000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$) expanding into ISM densities $n = 0.001\text{--}10\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ with radiative cooling, calculating synthetic X-ray spectra via XSPEC.
papers.reason: The paper reports the discovery of the first nova super-remnant (NSR) candidate in X-rays surrounding the Galactic recurrent nova V745 Scorpii using eROSITA, probing recurrent nova ejecta-ISM interaction and shock energetics.

papers.title: How common are extreme scattering events?: First large sample from the ASKAP VAST survey
papers.result: The authors identify 236 ESE candidates (72 gold, 76 silver, 88 bronze) with flux variations $\ge 2$. Under a characteristic scale $a \approx 1\;\mathrm{AU}$ and scale height $\approx 1\;\mathrm{kpc}$, the inferred core electron density is $n_0 \gtrsim 100\;\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, implying an overpressured plasma lens with $P/k > 10^2 T_e\;\mathrm{K\,cm^{-3}}$. The measured ESE event rates at $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ over a $12,500\;\mathrm{deg^2}$ footprint are $0.003\;(0.006)\;\mathrm{events/source/year}$ and $0.006\;(0.012)\;\mathrm{events/year/deg^2}$ for the gold (gold+silver) samples, with light curves strongly favoring overdense lenses ($\alpha > 0$).
papers.problem: Extreme scattering events (ESEs) are probe tools for $\sim\mathrm{AU}$-scale interstellar medium structures, but historically only $\sim 30$ events were known over four decades. Determining their true spatial distribution, event rates, density profiles (overdense vs underdense), and resolving the extreme overpressure crisis in the warm ionized medium have remained unconstrained due to small sample sizes.
papers.method: Candidates were selected from 24,590 bright compact sources in the ASKAP VAST $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ survey using flux variation ratio $\ge 2$, ML filtering, comparison with VLASS $3\;\mathrm{GHz}$, and dynamic spectrum evolution ($S_\nu \propto \nu^\alpha$). Events were modeled using a 1D plasma lens parameterized by $\alpha = (\lambda^2 r_e N_0 D_L)/(\pi a^2)$, normalized source size $\beta_{\rm src}$, transverse velocity $v$, and unlensed fraction $f_{\rm unlens}$, combined with a Matérn-3/2 red noise kernel sampled via MCMC.
papers.reason: The paper presents the first large, statistical sample of 236 extreme scattering events (ESEs) from the ASKAP VAST survey, expanding the historical sample by more than a factor of five. This provides key constraints on AU-scale ionized plasma structures, overpressure states in the ISM, and the propagation environments of compact radio transients.

papers.title: Faint and Fast Transients from Double Detonations of Low Mass White Dwarfs
papers.result: Low-mass WD double detonations ($M_{\rm tot} \sim 0.525\text{--}0.6\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm shell} \sim 0.15\text{--}0.3\,M_\odot$) produce low $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ yields (core produces $\lesssim 5\times 10^{-3}\,M_\odot$ for thin shells, up to $\sim 10^{-2}\,M_\odot$), peak luminosities $L_{\rm peak} \sim 1.4\times 10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($M_{\rm peak} \sim -15$ to $-17\,\mathrm{mag}$), rapid rise times ($5\text{--}10\,\mathrm{days}$), and fast post-peak declines ($\,\Delta m_{10} \sim 1\text{--}1.75\,\mathrm{mag}$ in 10 days). Ejecta retain up to $28\%$ unburned carbon with low expansion velocities ($v_{\rm Ca} \sim 5300\text{--}13300\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$).
papers.problem: Predicting the nucleosynthetic yields, light curve shapes, and spectral features of double detonations in low-mass white dwarfs with thick helium shells to test whether they account for faint and fast-declining transients such as Ca-rich transients or SNe Iax.
papers.method: Hydrodynamic modeling using the 1D moving-mesh code `Cattails` coupled with a 13-isotope reaction network from `pynucastro`, followed by synthetic light curves and spectra computed via the Monte Carlo radiation transport code `Sedona` under the assumption of homologous expansion.
papers.reason: The paper presents 1D hydrodynamic simulations and Monte Carlo radiative transfer of double detonations in low-mass white dwarfs ($M_{\rm tot} \sim 0.6\,M_\odot$), providing critical synthetic signatures (faint, fast-evolving transients with unburned carbon and narrow absorption lines) for unusual thermonuclear explosions like Ca-rich transients.

papers.title: Effects of Dust in Electron-Capture Supernovae: Difficulty in Explaining Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients
papers.result: Standard ECSN models with dusty winds cannot simultaneously reproduce the light curves and colors of ILRTs: the intrinsic drop in input luminosity after the plateau causes $r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$ to shrink, triggering a runaway increase in optical depth $\tau_V$ and causing the optical luminosity to plummet by orders of magnitude; attempting to flatten the decline using dense CSM shock interaction ($L_{s,\rm rad} \propto t^{-0.3}$) requires $\dot{M}_{\rm dense} \simeq 9.7 \times 10^{-3}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and produces excessively red post-plateau colors ($B - V > 4$) that contradict observed ILRT colors ($B - V \lesssim 1.2\text{--}1.6$).
papers.problem: Theoretical ECSN models from super-AGB progenitors predict plateau luminosities ($10^{41}\text{--}10^{42}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$) and post-plateau drops that are too luminous and steep compared to smooth, low-luminosity ILRTs like SN 2008S and NGC 300-OT.
papers.method: The authors develop a semi-analytical radiative transfer framework coupling ECSN light curves with Chevalier-type shock interaction luminosity ($L_s(t) \simeq \frac{1}{2}\dot{M} v_s^3 / v_w \propto t^{-0.3}$), amorphous carbon dust grain growth limited by gas recombination and growth timescales ($f_{\rm dust}(r,t)$), dynamic dust sublimation ($r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$), and light-travel time boxcar smoothing ($2R/c$).
papers.reason: This paper investigates whether electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) coupled with circumstellar dust attenuation and CSM interaction can account for intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs), which directly connects to CSM interaction and supernova plateau physics.

papers.title: Measuring the magnetization profiles of galaxy groups and clusters
papers.result: For a coherence length $l_c = 10\,\mathrm{kpc}$ within $R < R_{200c}$, the 95% upper limits on the line-of-sight rms magnetic field are $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}} < 3.9\text{--}11.6\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ for DESI BGS groups and $< 2.3\text{--}6.4\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ for RASS clusters, scaling as $l_c^{-1/2}$; the 95% lower limits on plasma beta are $\beta > 0.31$ and $\beta > 11$ respectively, derived via $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}}(R)=B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)\sqrt{L(R)/l_c}$ with $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)=\mathrm{RM}_{\mathrm{rest}}(R)/[0.812\,\mathrm{DM}(R)]\,\mu\mathrm{G}$.
papers.problem: Disentangling the severe baryon-magnetic field degeneracy in Faraday rotation measure (RM), which integrates $n_e B_\parallel$, and circumventing sign cancellations to measure the magnetic field profiles and plasma $\beta$ in galaxy groups and clusters.
papers.method: Cross-correlating $\mathrm{RM}^2$ from SPICE-RACS DR2 with foreground tracers (DESI BGS groups and RASS clusters), dividing by electron column density profiles from joint FRB DM–$z$ and ACT kSZ calibrations ($N_e(R)=\tau(R)/\sigma_T$), and scaling by chord length $L(R)=2\sqrt{(2R_{200c})^2-R^2}$ under coherence length $l_c$ via $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}}(R)=B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)\sqrt{L(R)/l_{c}}$.
papers.reason: The paper leverages the FRB DM-redshift relation and kSZ measurements to break the baryon-magnetic field degeneracy in RM stacks, obtaining magnetization and plasma beta constraints in galaxy groups and clusters.

papers.title: On the Interpretation of Tests of the Horizon Area Law
papers.result: Simulated gravitational-wave signals from an equal-mass, nonspinning binary boson star merger prompt-collapse scenario scaled to total mass $M = 71.5 M_\odot$ at network signal-to-noise ratio $\rho_{\rm network} = 80.2$ pass the observational horizon area-law consistency test (inferring $\Delta A = (A_f - A_i)/A_f > 0$) with confidence between $80\%$ and $92\%$, despite the premerger components lacking event horizons.

Component and remnant parameters are converted to horizon areas via the Kerr formula $A = 8\pi M^2 (1 + \sqrt{1 - |\vec{\chi}|^2})$.

The IMBHs grow from $10^3\ \mathrm{M_\odot}$ to $M_1 = 1.086 \times 10^5\ \mathrm{M_\odot}$ and $M_2 = 4.119 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{M_\odot}$, and the resulting gravitational-wave recoil kick of $v_{\mathrm{recoil}} \approx 174.9\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ ejects the remnant from the NSC while keeping it gravitationally bound to the host galaxy.
papers.problem: Isolated IMBHs in dwarf galaxies suffer severe orbital stalling (at $50\text{--}200\ \mathrm{pc}$) due to weak dynamical friction in shallow potentials and fail to grow through gas accretion or harden via stellar scattering within a Hubble time.
papers.method: Hydrodynamical $N$-body simulations combining the high-resolution multiphase ISM and stellar feedback model GRIFFIN with the Ketju regularized gravitational dynamics code (including PN 3.5 corrections for GW inspiral), implementing sink particle gas accretion with $r_{\mathrm{acc}} = 0.5\ \mathrm{pc}$ subjected to angular momentum threshold $l < \sqrt{G M_{\mathrm{BH}} r_{\mathrm{acc}}}$.
papers.reason: This paper investigates the dynamical sinking, accretion growth, and binary coalescence of intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) within nuclear star clusters (NSCs) during dwarf-galaxy mergers, which lacks substantial connection to core high-energy transient astrophysical mechanisms such as FRBs/PRSs, supernova central engines, shock breakouts, relativistic jets, or high-energy neutrino emissions.
